body.translated_text: <s>Dīpaṃkarabhadra</s>'s <s>Guhyasamājamaṇḍalavidhi</s> (Procedure for the <s>Guhyasamāja Maṇḍala</s>)
Homage to <s>Vajrasattva</s>!

children.translated_text: Freed from the obscuration of the knowable and the rest, endowed with the mirror of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom) and the rest,
having bowed to the sacred wheel of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>'s secret, I speak of that from my recollection. ||1||
By the procedure of the glorious <s>Samāja</s> assembly, in accordance with the tradition of the wheel lineage,
one who has been consecrated by the <s>guru</s>, beginning with the water [initiation] and ending with the permission, ||2||
for the attainment of reality in this secret wheel, through the secret-<s>prajñā</s> (wisdom-consort) consecration,
a knower of secrets, knowing the reality of <s>yoga</s>, understanding the reality of the junction of the three vehicles, ||3||
knowledgeable about the division, according to tantric procedure, of <s>vidyās</s> (spells), heart-<s>mantras</s>, <s>mudrās</s> (seals),
and the threefold <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and of common and uncommon <s>siddhis</s> (attainments), ||4||
abiding in the <s>samaya</s>-<s>saṃvara</s> (commitment vow), devoted to the <s>prajñā</s>-yoga (wisdom-yoga) practice,
knowing the application of <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>, fit for accomplishing the welfare of beings, ||5||
even one endowed with firmness in <s>yoga</s> and the like, if not possessing the stated qualities,

children.text: sattvārthe naiva bhavyo yat sadbhis taiḥ syur guṇā hy amī || 6
children.translated_text: is not fit for the welfare of beings, for those qualities belong to the noble ones. ||6||
Compassionate, of excellent vows, devoted to recitation, faithful, knowing the profound reality,
having performed the preliminary practice, established in one's own wheel, one should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s>. ||7||
In some agreeable place, anointed with true sandalwood and the like,
strewn with fragrant flowers, having settled there early in the morning, ||8||
in the purification of the gates of liberation, on the moon in the heart, [visualizing] the brilliant syllable <s>maṃ</s>,
for the increase of the auspicious, one should perform confession and the like. ||9||
Standing before the <s>Buddhas</s> born in all directions and three times,
having made worship in due order with offerings such as forms arising from the radiance of the heart, ||10||
whatever evil deeds done in the three times, arising from mere false conceptions of mine,
like a dream within a dream and the like—all of it I confess three times. ||11||
Whatever wholesome and good [merit] belongs to the <s>Buddhas</s>, noble Bodhisattvas, and <s>Āryas</s>, and to others—
rejoicing in all of it without remainder, I dedicate it toward <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). ||12||
I beseech all the <s>Buddhas</s>, giving assurance to all aspirations:
may the faultless [<s>Dharma</s>], established in the space of teaching, shine forth in the entire world! ||13||

body.text:
śuddhaniḥśeṣasaṃkalpān pratyātmānandavedinaḥ |
sambuddhān śaraṇaṃ yāmi svaparārthaphalapradān 14
body.translated_text: I go for refuge to the <s>Sambuddhas</s> (fully awakened ones), whose conceptions are entirely pure, who experience inner bliss, who bestow the fruit of one's own and others' welfare. ||14||

children.translated_text: The true <s>Dharma</s> of all noble beings, in its entirety, consisting of scripture and realization,
inconceivable, the basis of excellent attainments—I take refuge in it. ||15||
Having attained assurance, irreversible, endowed with fruits such as the outflow and the rest,
and also born of the secret consecration—I have gone to that assembly for refuge. ||16||
The true path of the sons of the Lord of Sages, the practice that awakens to infinite supreme [<s>bodhi</s>]—
with the true understanding that all <s>Buddhas</s> are the Self, I have now resorted to this. ||17||
The abode of infinite wisdom-nectar that destroys all obscurations,
for the awakening from the views of delusion—I set my mind on <s>bodhi</s> in its entirety. ||18||
And from <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind) comes Buddhahood; because the fruit-cause is unattached,
because reality is to be known by oneself—I am of the nature of emptiness-wisdom. ||19||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>—I am of the nature of the <s>vajra</s> of emptiness-<s>jñāna</s> (knowledge).

body.text: hūṅkāraṃ cāpy athoṣṇīṣān śāśvatādikam eva ca ||
body.translated_text: And then <s>hūṃkāra</s> (the syllable <s>hūṃ</s>), and the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance), and the eternal and the rest,
for the purpose of protection, established in the wrathful wheel, one should meditate, crushing obstacles. ||20||

children.translated_text: Then one should meditate on the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality)—triangular, white, situated above,
brilliant as the revolving discs of the directions, within which are lotuses and <s>vajras</s> below. ||21||
There, arising from the wrathful wheel of the syllable <s>bhrūṃ</s>, born together with the <s>vidyā</s> (consort) and the eternal [one],
radiating floods of <s>Buddhas</s> pervading all of space, endowed with a square [form] and the like, ||22||
mounted upon the moon and the sun, the universal lotus-seat of deities,
adorned with every kind of true jewel—one should visualize the mansion. ||23||
Endowed with the characteristics of vowels, with rays of consonants beginning with <s>ka</s>,
on the central moon-seat, having visualized the mind as the wisdom-moon, ||24||
there, the <s>vajra</s> arising from the primordial heart, red, endowed with the primordial heart[-mantra],
for the purpose of conferring the body of the <s>Jina</s> (conqueror)—he himself possessing the self-identification with that, ||25||
crystal-moon [complexion] on the body, with a root [dark blue] face, blue on the left, the other red,
excellent in every form, with ornaments of true qualities, and [celestial] garments, ||26||
two-armed, embracing the true <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom-consort), firmly seated in <s>vajra</s>-<s>paryaṅka</s> (cross-legged posture),
holding a <s>vajra</s>-sword in the right arm, and a true gem-lotus in the left, ||27||
consisting of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), the glorious one, the resort of the world's prosperity,
one should visualize oneself as <s>Samantabhadra</s>, radiating splendor. ||28||
Having seen that world as the vessel [of beings] to be tamed through great passion,
by the sound of sexual union, one should install within oneself the host of <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors). ||29||
Those true <s>vidyās</s> (female deities) such as <s>Locanā</s> and the rest, having the nature of sense-objects such as form,
having emanated the nine goddesses, one should install them within one's own <s>vidyā</s> (consort). ||30||
In the lotus-pistil of one's own consort, the <s>maṇḍala</s> born of sexual union,
having magically created it, one should cause the entire world to enter for the purpose of consolation. ||31||
With the true friends who are <s>Buddhas</s> pervading space, born from the fluid within one's own <s>vajra</s>,
one should serve them for the purpose of irreversibility, in order to obtain the fruit of true knowledge. ||32||

children.text: āśvastaṃ taj jagad dṛṣṭvā bījaiś cātaḥ svabhāvajaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having seen that world consoled, and then with seed-syllables born of their own nature,
one should emanate all beings, born from the mind-nature of the world. ||33||
The six beginning with <s>Kṣitigarbha</s>, having the nature of the eye and the other [senses],

children.text: kṣiṃ jraṃ khaṃ gaṃ skaṃ ity ebhiḥ saṃ-bījāc ca yathākramam || 34
children.translated_text: with [the syllables] <s>kṣiṃ</s>, <s>jraṃ</s>, <s>khaṃ</s>, <s>gaṃ</s>, <s>skaṃ</s>, and from the <s>saṃ</s>-seed, respectively in order, ||34||
the six such as <s>Rūpavajra</s> and the rest, born of the outer and inner natures,

children.text: jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ khaṃ ity etai raṃ-bījāc ca bahiḥ sthitān ||35
children.translated_text: with <s>jaḥ</s>, <s>hūṃ</s>, <s>vaṃ</s>, <s>hoḥ</s>, <s>khaṃ</s>, and from the <s>raṃ</s>-seed, stationed outside, ||35||
and the <s>vidyās</s> (female deities) such as <s>Locanā</s> and the rest, born of the natures of earth and the other [elements],

children.text: lāṃ māṃ pāṃ tām iti tv ebhir jagaddharmātmatattvajāḥ || 36
children.translated_text: with <s>lāṃ</s>, <s>māṃ</s>, <s>pāṃ</s>, <s>tāṃ</s>—born from the reality of the world's <s>dharmas</s>, ||36||
and the <s>Sambuddhas</s> (fully awakened ones) such as the Eternal One and the rest, born of the natures of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) such as form,
with <s>buṃ</s>, <s>āṃ</s>, <s>jrīṃ</s>, and with <s>khaṃ</s> and <s>hūṃ</s>—one should emanate all <s>dharmas</s>. ||37||

children.text: oṃ āḥ hūṃ iti tac cittaṃ bhāsvaddhorbhyāṃ vidarbhitam |
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ āḥ hūṃ</s>—that mind, entwined by the two radiant arms,
placed within the interior of the secret lotus, for the purification of the gentle outflow, ||38||
and those, when the two bodies are liquefied by the fire of passion being kindled—
through the song of the goddesses of the directions, true friends, one should meditate as good incitements. ||39||

children.text: tvaṃ vajracitta bhuvaneśvara sattvadhāto trāyāhi māṃ ratimanojñā mahārthakāmaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'You, <s>Vajracitta</s> (vajra-mind), lord of the worlds, essence of beings—save me with great desires, delightful in passion;

children.text: kamāhi māṃ janaka sarvamahāgrabandho yadīcchase jīvitu mahya nātha || 40
children.translated_text: love me, O father, O great supreme bond of all—if you wish me to live, O lord!' ||40||
'You, <s>Vajrakāya</s> (vajra-body), beloved of many beings, wheel of noble purpose, foreseeing the supreme benefit of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening—

children.text: rāgeṇa rāgasamayāṃ mama kāmayasva yadīcchase jīvitu mahya nātha || 41
children.translated_text: with passion, desire me, one who is of the nature of the passion-<s>samaya</s>—if you wish me to live, O lord!' ||41||

children.text: tvaṃ vajravāca sakalasya hitānukampī lokārthakāryakaraṇe sadā saṃpravṛtta |
children.translated_text: 'You, <s>Vajravāca</s> (vajra-speech), compassionate for the welfare of all, always engaged in performing the work for the world's benefit—

children.text: kāmahi māṃ suratacarya samantabhadra yadīcchase jīvitu mahya nātha || 42
children.translated_text: love me, O <s>Samantabhadra</s>, in the practice of sexual union—if you wish me to live, O lord!' ||42||

children.text: tvaṃ vajrakāma samayāgra mahāhitārtha sambuddhavaṃśatilakaḥ samatānukampī |
children.translated_text: 'You, <s>Vajrakāma</s> (vajra-desire), foremost in commitment, acting for great benefit, ornament of the lineage of <s>Sambuddhas</s>, compassionate in equanimity—

children.text: kāmāhi māṃ guṇanidhiṃ bahuratnabhūtāṃ yadīcchase jīvitu mahya nātha || 43
children.translated_text: desire me, O treasury of virtues, one who is of the nature of many jewels—if you wish me to live, O lord!' ||43||
Due to the arousal and harmony, seeing that fluid as if a calamity,

children.text: māyāvad vastu saṃcintya svamantrārthaḥ punar bhavet || 44
children.translated_text: contemplating the thing as illusory, one should again become the meaning of one's own <s>mantra</s>. ||44||
Saffron-colored on the body, with a root [dark blue] face, blue on the left, white on the other [right],
with the appearance of a youth's ornaments, beautiful with the sole bliss of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), ||45||
two-armed, embracing the true <s>Prajñā</s>, holding one's own <s>Prajñā</s> with [the other] faces,
with a radiant sword, true arrows, a blue lotus, and a bow in hand, ||46||
the three worlds accomplished through emanations of radiating floods of <s>Buddhas</s>,
one should become <s>Mañjuvajra</s> himself, arising from the emblem born of one's own seed-syllable. ||47||
From attachment to existence, existence is endless; attachment to cessation brings calamity;
one who serves [beings] through illusion becomes of the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). ||48||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>—I am of the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

children.translated_text: Having produced the outflow through the true friends, by ripening one would attain omniscience;
the consecration of the eye and the rest [of the senses] is considered the preliminary practice (<s>upasādhana</s>). ||49||
With [the syllables for] earth-lord, <s>vajra</s>, space, world-lord, <s>skandha</s>, water, and <s>Bhadra</s>,
filling the eye and the other [senses] with those seed-syllables, one should assume the heroic [posture]. ||50||
The channels bearing <s>Dharma</s>-body, enjoyment-body, and emanation-body—the purposefulness for the world;
the consecration of mind-secret and the rest then becomes for the purpose of practice (<s>sādhana</s>). ||51||
On the moons at one's own heart, throat, and head, [visualizing] <s>hūṃ</s>, <s>āḥ</s>, <s>oṃ</s>, and <s>jāṃ</s>, the true lords,
stationed in the centers of the <s>vajra</s>, lotus, and wheel, meditating on the secrets of mind and the rest, ||52||
with rays of <s>Rūpavajra</s> and the rest—the flames of union with the <s>prajñā</s>-limbs held by their hearts—
worshipping all the <s>Vināyakas</s> (guides) pervading all directions and three times, ||53||
of those whose prosperity of purpose is accomplished, those who have gone to the heart, throat, and head—
<s>Cittavajra</s> (mind-<s>vajra</s>) and the rest—one should request them for that consecration. ||54||
'The glorious bearer of the <s>Cittavajra</s> (mind-<s>vajra</s>), made indestructible by the three <s>vajras</s>,
may he confer upon me today the status of consecration of the <s>Cittavajrin</s> (mind-<s>vajra</s>-holder)!' ||55||
'The <s>Buddhas</s> stationed in the ten directions, made indestructible by the three <s>vajras</s>,
may they confer upon me today the status of consecration of the <s>Cittavajrin</s>!' ||56||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>—I am of the nature of the <s>Cittavajra</s> (mind-<s>vajra</s>) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.translated_text: 'The <s>Dharma</s>, the glorious lord of the speech-path, made indestructible by the three <s>vajras</s>,
may he confer upon me today the status of consecration of the <s>Vāgvajrin</s> (speech-<s>vajra</s>-holder)!' ||57||
'The <s>Buddhas</s> stationed in the ten directions, made indestructible by the three <s>vajras</s>,
may they confer upon me today the status of consecration of the <s>Vāgvajrin</s>!' ||58||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>—I am of the nature of the <s>Vāgvajra</s> (speech-<s>vajra</s>) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.translated_text: 'The glorious bearer of the <s>Kāyavajra</s> (body-<s>vajra</s>), made indestructible by the three <s>vajras</s>,
may he confer upon me today the status of consecration of the <s>Kāyavajrin</s> (body-<s>vajra</s>-holder)!' ||59||
'The <s>Buddhas</s> stationed in the ten directions, made indestructible by the three <s>vajras</s>,
may they confer upon me today the status of consecration of the <s>Kāyavajrin</s>!' ||60||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>—I am of the nature of the <s>Kāyavajra</s> (body-<s>vajra</s>) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.translated_text: In the purification of the sixteen recollections, 'they confer'—thus it has been stated;
the consecration of the mind and the rest of that one has not been stated, as it is irrelevant to the context. ||61||
Having examined the characteristiclessness of the three secrets, through the union with the <s>māyā-prajñā</s> (illusory wisdom-consort) limbs,
in the purification of the gentle purity, the great practice (<s>mahāsādhana</s>) is prescribed. ||62||
Having summoned the lords stationed in the directions with the flame of the <s>jñānasattva</s> (wisdom-being) in the heart,
with the nectar-water from the filled pitcher, by the <s>vidyās</s> arising from their lord, ||63||
self-consecrated, the glorious lord, [with] the supreme crown of the family-lord,

children.text: niṣyandādyais tathā madhyaiḥ svābhāṃ prajñāṃ viśodhayet || 64
children.translated_text: by the outflow and the like, and also by the intermediate [methods], one should purify one's own <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom-consort). ||64||
At her head, heart, navel, secret [place], and the tips of her feet, atoms,
with <s>oṃ</s>, <s>hūṃ</s>, <s>svā</s>, <s>hṛd</s>, <s>āḥ</s>, and <s>hā</s>, having the nature of the families of the Eternal One and the rest, ||65||
having filled the eight-petaled lotus with the five <s>Sambuddhas</s>, with <s>hūṃ</s> and <s>āḥ</s>,
having purified them, with the <s>hūṃ</s>-true-<s>vajra</s> one should cause delight. ||66||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>—I am of the nature of the <s>vajra</s> of the delight of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.translated_text: With the radiations of the heart-moon-sword-heart, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> pervading space,
having installed within oneself the true form of the mind, situated on the <s>vajra</s>-lotus, ||67||
one's own wheel, having produced it by one's own seed-syllable and stabilized it there,
one should emanate it by this method into the worlds for the purification of ignorance. ||68||
Having summoned the lord <s>Akṣobhya</s>, the <s>Jina</s> who accomplishes the purpose of great hatred,
'<s>Vajra</s>-holder!'—thus having emanated him, of the radiance of an <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) gem, ||69||
white on the left side, red on the other, endowed with the arms of the primordial one,
having absorbed [him] into oneself, the glorious one, one should install him with all aspects. ||70||
'<s>Jina</s>-conqueror!'—thus, of the radiance of the primordial one, the lord who accomplishes the purpose of great delusion,
endowed with the true wheel and the rest—one should likewise meditate on the eastern moon-<s>maṇḍala</s>. ||71||
'Jewel-holder!'—thus the lord of jewels, of golden radiance, endowed with effort,
with true jewels and the rest, the lord of youthful aspect—on the south. ||72||
'<s>Ārolik</s>!'—thus the lord of speech, the lord who accomplishes the purpose of great passion,
of ruby-lotus radiance, with lotus and the rest, of youthful aspect—on the west. ||73||
'<s>Prajñā</s>-holder!'—thus the invincible lord <s>Amogha</s>, who accomplishes the purpose of great fierce envy,
of <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl) radiance, of youthful aspect—one should meditate with sword and the rest, on the north. ||74||
All with matted-hair crowns, united with their two respective <s>vidyās</s> (consorts),
with all ornaments and true garments—they should be meditated upon on the lotus-sun-<s>maṇḍala</s>. ||75||
'<s>Moharati</s> (Delusion-passion)!'—in the southeast, bestowing <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion), <s>upāya</s> (means), and the welfare of beings,
of the same form as the body-lord, <s>Locanā</s> should be [visualized] on her own moon-<s>maṇḍala</s>. ||76||
'<s>Dveṣarati</s> (Hatred-passion)!'—in the southwest, bestowing <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>praṇidhi</s> (aspiration), and desire,
eagerness for passion like the mind-lord—<s>Māmakī</s> on the moon-<s>maṇḍala</s>. ||77||
'<s>Rāgarati</s> (Passion-passion)!'—in the northwest, bestowing joy, power, and <s>samādhi</s>,
of the radiance of the speech-lord, pure in meaning—<s>Pāṇḍarā</s> on the moon-<s>maṇḍala</s>. ||78||
'<s>Vajrarati</s> (Vajra-passion)!'—in the northeast, accomplishing equanimity-wisdom,
of the same form as the jewel-lord—the delightful <s>Tārā</s> on the moon[-maṇḍala</s>]. ||79||

children.text: cakraṃ raktotpalaṃ divyaṃ paṅkajaṃ pītaṃ utpalam |
children.translated_text: A wheel, a red lotus, a divine lotus, a yellow lotus,

children.text: śiṣṭaṃ svādhipavad diṣṭaṃ cihnam āsāṃ kramād ataḥ || 80
children.translated_text: the rest as indicated by their respective lords—these are their emblems in order. ||80||
At the four corners beginning with the southeast, and on both sides of the eastern gate,
<s>Rūpā</s> (Form) and the rest, with mirror and the like, of the radiance of the body[-lord] and the rest, according to the three realities. ||81||
At the eastern gate, in wrathful cross-legged posture, radiant in the form of the mind-lord,
'Slayer of <s>Yama</s>!'—thus the destroyer of death, through the destruction of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and the knowable. ||82||
Of the radiance of the body-lord, terrible and fierce—at the southern gate, <s>Aparājita</s> (the Unconquered),
'Slayer of <s>Prajñā</s>[-enemies]!'—the destroyer of desire, through the removal of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) by self-vision. ||83||
Killer of death, birth, and sin—at the western gate, <s>Aśvakandhra</s> (Horse-neck),
'Slayer of the Lotus[-enemies]!'—the destroyer of desire, whirling fiercely in the radiance of the speech-lord. ||84||
Of the radiance of <s>Akṣobhya</s>, fiercely destroying obstacles—at the north, <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalin</s>,
'Slayer of Obstacles!'—thus, through the purification of the gate-action-<s>asura</s> (demon) enemies. ||85||
With frowning brows, upward-blazing hair, tawny brows, beards, and eyes,
With gaping mouths, lolling tongues, and fierce grins with protruding fangs, ||86||
these [deities] hold in their hands fierce hammers, staffs, lotuses, their own <s>vajras</s>, and so forth;
their bodies adorned with fierce serpent ornaments, embracing their own innate consorts (<s>vidyā</s>). ||87||
Having beheld the completed <s>maṇḍala</s> (<s>cakra</s>) from all sides with one's own nature,
[one should visualize] the <s>Buddhas</s> gathered in the form of the <s>maṇḍala</s> by the hook-rays of the heart-seed [syllable]. ||88||
Having seen the obstacles, driven them away with one's own obstacle-destroyers, and provided protection,
having offered the <s>arghya</s> (guest-water) consecrated with <s>mantras</s> and accompanied by flowers of moon and so forth, ||89||
having established that <s>maṇḍala</s> within the <s>maṇḍala</s>, empowered through eye, body, and so forth,

children.text: prāgvat siktaṃ ca tad dhyāyān niṣyandādyadhimātrataḥ || 90
children.translated_text: meditating on that [<s>maṇḍala</s>] as sprinkled as before, through the abundance of outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>) and so forth, ||90||
<s>Akṣobhya</s> [appears] on the crown of the <s>Buddhas</s>; the rest [receive consecration] from their own lords;
the door-guardians are known [to be consecrated] by the Lord of Body (<s>Akṣobhya</s>), the Lord of Speech, and the Lord of Mind. ||91||
Having thus consecrated, [the practitioner,] established within the lotus of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) by the radiances of one's own heart,
[should worship] with rays of <s>Rūpavajrā</s> and the others, arising from the pores [of the body], consisting of forms and so forth, ||92||
released from the radiance of the pinnacled mansion (<s>kūṭāgāra</s>), spreading throughout space,

children.text: sampūjya svaṃ munīndrāṃś ca pūjyapūjātmako bhavet || 93
children.translated_text: having worshipped oneself and the lords of sages, one should become the essence of the worshipped and the worship. ||93||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, I am the essence of the <s>vajra</s>-nature of the worship of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.translated_text: One should praise the <s>maṇḍala</s> with all <s>dharmas</s>, through the forms of the perfectly awakened ones who are one's own self,
the five wisdoms (<s>jñānas</s>) through <s>mudrās</s>, the hundred-and-five families, the triad. ||94||
O <s>Akṣobhyavajra</s>, great wisdom, <s>vajra</s>-realm, greatly wise one!
O triple <s>maṇḍala</s>, triple <s>vajra</s>-summit, <s>Ghoṣavajra</s>—homage to you! ||95||
O <s>Vairocana</s>, greatly pure, <s>Vajraśānta</s>, great delight!
O foremost of the primordially luminous, supreme <s>Deśavajra</s>—homage to you! ||96||
O <s>Ratnarāja</s>, profoundly deep, space-<s>vajra</s>, pure as the sky!
Naturally pure, unstained, <s>Kāyavajra</s>—homage to you! ||97||
O <s>Vajrāmita</s>, great king, free from conceptualization, holder of the space-<s>vajra</s>!
Having attained the perfection of passion (<s>rāga-pāramitā</s>), <s>Bhāṣavajra</s>—homage to you! ||98||
O <s>Amoghavajra</s>, perfectly awakened, fulfiller of all wishes!
Born of pure nature, <s>Vajrasattva</s>—homage to you! ||99||
Moon, sun, water, medicine, incense, wind, fire—revolving in the <s>maṇḍala</s>,
empowered by <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>), with flames, consecrated by the three realities (<s>tattvas</s>), ||100||
having meditated with <s>vajra</s>-tongue extended by the <s>Hūṃ</s> syllable, [the offering] filled with the nectar of wisdom (<s>jñānāmṛta</s>),
one should satisfy the entire <s>maṇḍala</s> within the moon of the heart with that [nectar]. ||101||
By the lords emanated from the rays of the heart, free from false conceptualization,
having made the world <s>Buddha</s>-natured, one should establish [them] within the heart-seed [syllable]. ||102||
Established within the <s>varaṭā</s> (canopy) of the heart-emblem, in the form of the moon-heart-<s>bindu</s>,
meditating on one's own luminous mind, one should illuminate the <s>jñānasattva</s> (wisdom-being). ||103||
Having awakened the mind-<s>vajra</s>, speech-<s>vajra</s>, and body-<s>vajra</s> through a garland of rays,
one should meditate on that [stream] established in the heart, the channel carrying one's own wisdom-nectar. ||104||

children.text: antas tanum ataḥ sarvāṃ tayābhāsya samantataḥ |
children.translated_text: From that, having illuminated the entire inner body on all sides with that [stream],
fulfilling the purpose of the world with arrays of radiance [streaming] against the hair [i.e., outward], ||105||
or meditating on one's own subtle emblem, the <s>vidyā</s> (consort) stationed at the tip of the nose,
the <s>maṇḍala</s> of sages, self-experienced, luminous through the embrace of true <s>prajñā</s>, ||106||
having seen the sign of stability, [one should practice] expansion through the signs of those rays;

children.text: buddhair nānāvidhaiś cihnair vidadhīta punaḥ punaḥ || 107
children.translated_text: with <s>Buddhas</s> and various emblems, one should perform [this] again and again. ||107||
From the true <s>vajra</s> of body, speech, and mind, [emanating] rays of five true wisdoms,
one should perform the expanding <s>mantra</s> recitation, simultaneously or in sequence. ||108||
The <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>vajra</s>, lotus, <s>dharma</s>, and [karma], pervading the body-, speech-, and mind-<s>vajra</s>,

children.text: nilayaṃ tad dṛḍhīkurvañ jñānakāyaṃ spharañ japet || 109
children.translated_text: stabilizing that abode, expanding the wisdom-body, one should recite. ||109||
One should utter the <s>mantra</s>, expanding with the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), contracted by extension,
performing the recitation through the expansion and contraction of body and so forth, in sequence or out of sequence. ||110||

children.text: uccāryaivaṃ viyad vyāpya kāyādyais taiḥ svaraśmibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus uttered, pervading space with body and the rest through their own rays,
as before, worthy of true worship of the mind, releasing the stream of <s>vidyā</s> from the breath, ||111||
subjugated by the bliss-possession of the deeply embraced and radiant <s>vidyā</s>,
one should finally establish within oneself the flood of <s>Buddhas</s> of extended non-wisdom. ||112||
Through convictions of outflow and so forth, the <s>yogas</s> born from <s>bindu</s>, subtlety, and the three secrets,

children.text: dhyeyā mṛdvādibhir bhedair yogāḥ sevādivat tathā || 113
children.translated_text: should be meditated upon with distinctions of mild and so forth, like the practice of service (<s>sevā</s>) and so forth. ||113||
From grasping the reality within one's own heart, [arising] from the cycle of a limited mind,
one should worship the <s>maṇḍala</s>, invoking it with songs sung by the retinue of <s>Locanā</s> and the others. ||114||
One should cause to descend the stream of mind-water, moistened by the <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) on the moon at the crown,
performing the delight of body, speech, and mind according to the proper method. ||115||
Having thus rested, performed the recitation, and completed worship and so forth, the wise one
should dismiss the <s>Buddhas</s> established in the three realities, free from attachment. ||116||

children.text: evaṃ tattvadṛśā muktaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ vilokya ca |
children.translated_text: Having thus beheld the entire world as liberated through the vision of reality,
one should dedicate the aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>) with compassion for their benefit. ||117||
Rising from <s>samādhi</s>, bearing the pride of the Lord,
while going about in conduct, one should worship with the sense-fields of a perfectly awakened one. ||118||
The glorious <s>Mañjuvajra</s>, the self of all, [experiencing] sense-objects that accord with their natural domain,
thus cultivating sense-objects established in their respective purity, ||119||
those whose nature is eternality and so forth, established in the <s>dharma</s> of one's own self,
in the form of the glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>, endowed with pure being, ||120||
one should accomplish all activities, free from false conceptualization;
this is the true, infinite worship of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, ever immeasurable for the accomplished <s>yogin</s>. ||121||
On the moon of one's own heart, [meditating on] the lord of one's own <s>maṇḍala</s>, with one's own seed-syllables, one's own sustenance,
supported by the realities of one's own heart, rendered immortal by all the <s>Buddhas</s>, ||122||
pure through the nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, consecrated by the three realities,
one should worship by delighting the true <s>maṇḍala</s> of one's own presiding deity. ||123||
The external <s>homa</s> (fire offering) can be inferred from this; but the mental [<s>homa</s>] is from mind alone;
this unsurpassed [<s>homa</s>] is that which is burned by the fuel-mass of the fire of wisdom (<s>jñānāgni</s>). ||124||
Thus, with all desires, [one should worship] oneself, born of the nature of one's own presiding deity,

children.text: parāṃś ca pūjayed evaṃ samayaḥ sugatair mataḥ || 125
children.translated_text: and should worship others likewise—this is the <s>samaya</s> (commitment) held by the <s>Sugatas</s>. ||125||

children.text: tat tat kāyādi yat karma sarvabuddhāṃs tu pūjayan |
children.translated_text: Whatever action of body and so forth is performed, worshipping all <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: anurūpaṃ jagat kāryaṃ kuryān nityaṃ samāhitaḥ || 126
children.translated_text: one should always perform, with concentration, the appropriate benefit for the world. ||126||
Whatever great action of body and speech, consisting of <s>mudrā</s> and <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: tat tat karma samāsādya sarvabuddhāṃs tu pūjayet || 127
children.translated_text: undertaking each such action, one should worship all <s>Buddhas</s>. ||127||
Conceptions focused on a single object, appearing in various forms,
giving rise to liberation, suffering, and happiness—all actions arise from this, ||128||
therefore, auspicious and inauspicious actions of body and so forth, born of conceptualization—
how can there be such conceptualization in wisdom free from all true conceptualization? ||129||
The true <s>maṇḍala</s>-holder of <s>Amoghavajra</s>, for the purpose of awakening the <s>samaya</s>,
having meditated on the <s>vajra</s>-space of heart-action, should consecrate with complete purity. ||130||
In cases of faults such as disrespect toward the guru, one should always bring food offerings;
while established in one's own <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should perform external bathing according to the consecration method. ||131||

children.text: sandhyāntare 'pi pūjādi japaṃ kṛtvā tu pūrvavat |
children.translated_text: Also at twilight, having performed worship and recitation as before,
with the true <s>maṇḍala</s> within one's heart, one should sleep, endowed with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion). ||132||
At the time of rising, the glorious one, prompted by the songs of the goddesses,

children.text: prātar utthāya prāgvat tu saṃjaped ādikarmikaḥ || 133
children.translated_text: having risen in the morning, the beginner should recite as before. ||133||
Endowed with <s>mantra</s> discipline and vows, empowered through eye, body, and so forth,
having somewhat entered into wisdom, one should recite diligently at the twilight junctions. ||134||
Having perfectly accomplished all aspects, performing expansion and contraction,
one who has somewhat attained mastery of wisdom should constantly rely on <s>yoga</s>. ||135||
One who has attained mastery of perfect wisdom, while meditating, should perform activities for the world's benefit,
with the three true <s>maṇḍalas</s>, in reflected forms, to the ends of the atomic elements of realms. ||136||

children.text: saṃsiddhāv asakṛl labdhvā yogī nimittam eva tu |
children.translated_text: When the <s>yogin</s> has repeatedly obtained the sign of accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>),

children.text: tritattvāṃ vidhivat pūjāṃ kṛtvā maṇḍalam ālikhet || 137
children.translated_text: having performed worship of the three realities according to the proper method, one should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s>. ||137||

children.text: cakrastho vidhivaj japtvā svayaṃ vādhyeṣito 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: Established in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, having recited according to the method, whether self-motivated or requested [by others],
even while striving for the benefit of others, having obtained the sign, one should draw [the <s>maṇḍala</s>]. ||138||

children.text: cakrimantraṃ japel lakṣaṃ lakṣam vā svādhidaivatam |
children.translated_text: One should recite the <s>maṇḍala</s>-holder's <s>mantra</s> one hundred thousand times, or one hundred thousand [times] of one's own presiding deity;

children.text: anyeṣām ayutaṃ samyak cakriṇāṃ vājñayā likhet || 139
children.translated_text: for the others, ten thousand properly—the <s>maṇḍala</s>-holders should draw by the [master's] command. ||139||
With emanations pregnant with the three realities, and others pregnant with the heart-seed [syllable],
one should extract the name-<s>mantras</s>, with syllables bearing <s>anusvāra</s> and so forth. ||140||
Named body, speech, and mind secrets, of the great nature of action-<s>dharma</s>,

children.text: triguhyā samayā mudrā bījaṃ hṛdayam ucyate || 141
children.translated_text: the three secrets, <s>samaya</s>, <s>mudrā</s>, seed-syllable, and heart [<s>mantra</s>]—these are said [to be the types]. ||141||
The action-performer is the <s>vidyā</s> as proclaimed, from the incitement of pacification and so forth;

children.text: mālāmantrāś ca vidyoktā sarvathā tāṃ japet budhaḥ || 142
children.translated_text: the garland-<s>mantras</s> too are proclaimed by the <s>vidyā</s>—in all cases, the wise one should recite that. ||142||
Having performed recitation as appropriate and obtained permission from one's own lord,
having folded the cessation-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw from the purity of one's own mind. ||143||

children.text: vighnān utsārya saṃkīlyābhyukṣya kṣmāṃ prārthya yācayet |
children.translated_text: Having expelled obstacles, staked [the ground], sprinkled it, and made supplication to the earth,
having performed the threefold <s>samādhi</s>, and having [ritually] caused the <s>Buddhas</s> and others to take up residence, ||144||

children.text: dattvā balyargham āpūjya homair āpyāyya khe nyaset |
children.translated_text: having offered <s>bali</s> (ritual food) and <s>arghya</s> (guest-water), worshipped, and nourished [them] through <s>homa</s> (fire offering), one should place [them] in the sky;

children.text: khānayet kṣmāṃ sunirvighnāṃ gartāpūre 'pi ayaṃ kramaḥ || 145
children.translated_text: one should dig the earth, well cleared of obstacles—this same procedure [applies] also to filling the pit. ||145||
Having previously practiced the service [stage], the <s>yogin</s> of <s>Mañjuvajra</s>-identity,
having consecrated the <s>maṇḍala</s> site, accompanied by portable offerings, ||146||

children.text: duṣṭān nikṛntayed evaṃ yogād vā svādhidaivatāt | 147
children.translated_text: one should thus cut down the wicked, whether through <s>yoga</s> or through one's own presiding deity. ||147||

body.translated_text: established in the <s>yoga</s> of the obstacle-enemy <s>maṇḍala</s>, should perform one's own consecration;

children.text: oṃ bhūḥ kham iti mantreṇa viyadbhūtāṃ vasundharām |
children.translated_text: With the <s>mantra</s> '<s>Oṃ bhūḥ kham</s>,' [transforming] the earth into sky-nature,

children.text: hūṃ laṃ hūṃ iti vajrātma kṣmāṃ kṛtvā tām adhiṣṭhayet || 148
children.translated_text: '<s>Hūṃ laṃ hūṃ</s>'—having made the earth of <s>vajra</s>-nature, one should empower it: ||148||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ medinī vajrībhava vajrabandha hūṃ</s>.

children.translated_text: As before, with the nature of the obstacle-destroying <s>yoga</s>, delighting in the service and other [stages] from beginning to end,

children.text: ādiyogī svacakraṃ tu protsṛjyāntāmṛtaś ca saḥ || 149
children.translated_text: the beginning <s>yogin</s>, having released his own <s>maṇḍala</s> and [being one] whose end is nectar, ||149||
with the nature of the foremost <s>yoga</s> of the <s>maṇḍala</s>-king, performing the excellent actions of <s>maṇḍala</s>-ritual,
the foremost <s>yogin</s> of the action-king—this is the supreme threefold <s>samādhi</s>. ||150||
The <s>ācārya</s> (master), established in this <s>yoga</s>, being the embodiment of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
of naturally pure <s>vajra</s>-nature, situated in the center of the <s>maṇḍala</s>-ground, ||151||
the hero holding <s>vajra</s> and bell, should be requested [by the assistants]; having created the three <s>maṇḍalas</s>,
with companions holding foremost <s>vajra</s> and bell, embodying eternality and so forth: ||152||
'Teach the supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>, which is the peace of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the abode of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
the supreme selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>! ||153||
Complete with all marks, free from all [distinguishing] marks,
foremost of the body of <s>Samantabhadra</s>—proclaim the supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>! ||154||
Born of the foremost peaceful <s>dharma</s>, purifying wisdom-conduct,
foremost of the speech of <s>Samantabhadra</s>—proclaim the supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>! ||155||
The great mind of all beings, pure, naturally stainless,
foremost of the mind of <s>Samantabhadra</s>—proclaim, O charioteer of the <s>maṇḍala</s>!' ||156||
Thereupon, the glorious <s>Mañjurāj</s> (<s>Mañjuśrī</s>), enraged, seeing the realm of beings enveloped in darkness,

children.text: hūṃ vajrottiṣṭheti svakṣaś cakram utkṣipya nirmitam || 157
children.translated_text: '<s>Hūṃ</s>, arise, O <s>vajra</s>!'—with his own eye, lifting up the created <s>maṇḍala</s>, ||157||
with eyes of <s>maṭ</s>-syllable, moon, and sun, illuminating all paths and directions,
the wise one, surveying the world, should circumambulate the <s>maṇḍala</s>-ground. ||158||
With <s>vajras</s> blazing at the soles of the feet, intent on brandishing the <s>vajra</s>,
dancing the playful <s>vajra</s>-step, with protruding fangs, uttering '<s>Hūṃ</s>!' ||159||
One should drive away the hosts of wicked ones—the obstacle-<s>maṇḍalas</s> of gods and others:
'Listen, all hosts of obstacles established in body, speech, and mind! ||160||
I am the glorious <s>Mañjurava</s> (<s>Mañjughoṣa</s>), the master of the protection-<s>maṇḍala</s>!
With the <s>vajra</s> of blazing body, I shatter those born from the three bodies! ||161||

body.translated_text: Whoever transgresses [this boundary] shall be destroyed—there is no other [outcome]!'
Having taken possession of the ground, one should stake it for [the sake of] freedom from obstacles. ||162||

body.text: oṃ gha gha ghātaya 2 sarvaduṣṭān phaṭ kīlaya 2 sarvapāpān phaṭ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ vajrakīla vajradharo ājñāpayati sarvaduṣṭakāyavākcittavajraṃ kīlaya hūṃ phaṭ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ gha gha ghātaya ghātaya</s> (strike, strike) all wicked ones, <s>phaṭ</s>! <s>Kīlaya kīlaya</s> (stake, stake) all evil ones, <s>phaṭ</s>! <s>Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ</s>, O <s>Vajrakīla</s>! <s>Vajradhara</s> commands: stake the <s>vajra</s> of body, speech, and mind of all wicked ones! <s>Hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

children.translated_text: One should mentally stake the obstacle-enemy with [a stake having] a spike below and above,
and should destroy all hosts of obstacles established in the ten directions. ||163||
Having examined the ground, well cleared of obstacles, blazing with fierce flames,
having mentally made the boundary-walls and directional seals, one should [ritually] consecrate [the site]. ||164||
'O goddess, you are the witness of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the protectors,
in the special methods of practice, and in the <s>bhūmi-pāramitās</s> (perfections of the stages). ||165||
Just as the power of <s>Māra</s> was shattered by <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>, the protector,

children.text: tathā mārabalaṃ jitvā maṇḍalaṃ lelikhāmy aham || 166
children.translated_text: so, having conquered the power of <s>Māra</s>, I shall draw the <s>maṇḍala</s>.' ||166||

children.text: kṣmāṃ saṃlipya sugandhadyaiś citraiḥ puṣpaiḥ prakīrya ca |
children.translated_text: Having anointed the ground with fragrant [substances] and scattered it with colorful flowers,

children.text: candrādyaiś cakriṇāṃ sthāne prakuryān maṇḍalaṃ budhaḥ || 167
children.translated_text: the wise one should prepare the <s>maṇḍala</s> at the stations of the <s>maṇḍala</s>-holders with moon and so forth. ||167||
There, having invoked the true <s>maṇḍala</s>, having made the boundary-sealing and so forth,
one should consecrate the ritual vases with worship, praise, and the tasting of nectar. ||168||
The vases, with their fine necks covered with cloth, adorned with mango and other leaf-sprays,
one should consecrate the vases of the <s>maṇḍala</s> participants with their respective <s>mantras</s>. ||169||
Filled with the five grains, herbs, gems, perfumes, water, and an array of <s>maṇḍala</s> [offerings],
with a <s>vajra</s>-crown bound with garlands—one should recite with the lord of the <s>maṇḍala</s>. ||170||
Having offered <s>arghya</s> (guest-water), having fully worshipped, and having cast white flowers,
the lotus-vessel [containing] fine perfume and so forth, consecrated with incense, should be [placed] there. ||171||

children.text: pratidinaṃ trisandhyāsu baliṃ dattvā tathā japet |
children.translated_text: Daily, at the three twilight junctions, having offered <s>bali</s> (ritual food), one should likewise recite;
and they [the offerings should be placed] at the outer corners of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, with the victory [banner] to the right of the <s>maṇḍala</s>-lord. ||172||
Having cast water into the <s>arghya</s>-vessel for them, through that consecration,
There should be water-consecration (<s>jalābhiṣecana</s>) for oneself and all disciples. || 173

children.text: cakrapūjāṃ punaḥ kṛtvā dhūpam utkṣipya pāṇinā |
children.translated_text: Having again performed the <s>cakrapūjā</s> (wheel-worship) and casting incense upward with the hand,

children.text: cakreśaṃ prārthayed dhīmān buddhāṃś ca jānusaṃsthitaḥ || 174
children.translated_text: the wise one, seated on the knees, should petition the lord of the <s>cakra</s> (wheel) and the <s>Buddhas</s>. || 174
O <s>Bhagavan</s>, <s>Mañjusadvajra</s>, king of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), homage to you!
I wish to draw, O Lord, the <s>maṇḍala</s>, O one whose nature is compassion. || 175
For the sake of compassion toward the disciples, and for the worship of you all,

children.text: tan me bhaktasya bhagavan prasādaṃ kartum arhasi || 176
children.translated_text: therefore, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, be pleased to grant grace to me, your devotee. || 176
May the <s>Buddhas</s>, who bestow the purpose of the activity of the world-wheel, attend to me,

children.text: phalasthā bodhisattvāś ca yāś cānyā mantradevatāḥ || 177
children.translated_text: and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the fruit, and whatever other <s>mantra</s>-deities there are. || 177
The deities, the world-protectors (<s>lokapālas</s>), and the beings governed by awakening,
the beings delighting in the teaching, whoever possesses the <s>vajra</s>-eye. || 178
I, so-and-so, the great <s>vajra</s>-holder (<s>mahāvajrī</s>), the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the arising of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>,
shall draw for the purification of the world, with offerings according to my ability. || 179

children.text: anukampām upādāya saśiṣyasya tu tan mama |
children.translated_text: Taking up compassion toward me together with my disciples,

children.text: maṇḍale sahitāḥ sarve sāṃnidhyaṃ kartum arhatha || 180
children.translated_text: may you all, united in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, deign to be present. || 180

children.text: nimantryaivaṃ trivārāṃs tān kṛtvā pūjādikaṃ vibhoḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus invited them three times and performed worship and other rites for the Lord,
having protected them, going outside, [he should examine] his own disciples who bear garlands and offerings— || 181
those who are wise, of great enthusiasm, grateful, and free from pride,
of good family, possessed of virtues, faithful, endowed with beauty, complexion, and proper age, || 182
desirous and devoted, followers of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha) in <s>mantra</s>-practice—

children.text: virūpān nirguṇāṃś cāpi hīnān apy adhivāsayet || 183
children.translated_text: even those who are deformed, lacking virtues, or of low status, he should also consecrate (<s>adhivāsayet</s>). || 183

children.text: caturṇām apy anujñātaḥ parṣadāṃ maṇḍale vidhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The procedure in the <s>maṇḍala</s> is sanctioned for [members of] all four assemblies,
who are engaged in their own trainings and whose nature delights in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. || 184
Some enter this <s>maṇḍala</s> seeking <s>mantra</s>-accomplishment (<s>mantrasiddhi</s>),
others desiring merit, and yet others seeking the next world. || 185

children.text: paralokaṃ samuddiṣya śraddhāṃ kṛtvā ca bhūyasīm |
children.translated_text: Aiming at the next world and generating abundant faith,

children.text: praviśen maṇḍalaṃ dhīmān naihikam phalam īhayet || 186
children.translated_text: the wise one should enter the <s>maṇḍala</s> and seek the fruit of this [very life]. || 186
For one desiring worldly [fruit], the other-worldly [fruit] is not so [diminished];

children.text: paralokārthinaḥ puṃsaḥ puṣkalaṃ tv aihikaṃ phalam || 187
children.translated_text: for a person seeking the next world, the worldly fruit is indeed abundant. || 187

children.text: evam uktvā tu tān śiṣyān dhiyā svāntar niveśitān |
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to those disciples who are established within by wisdom,

children.text: prāgvad vajrābjasaṃśuddhān iha dvāre tu yācayet || 188
children.translated_text: purified as before by the <s>vajra</s> and the lotus, he should make request here at the door: || 188
I desire, O great Lord, the firm path of great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>). || 189

body.translated_text: You are my teacher, O one of great delight,

body.text:
dehi me samayaṃ tattvaṃ bodhicittaṃ ca dehi me |
buddhaṃ dharmaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca dehi me śaraṇatrayam

children.translated_text: Cause me to enter, O Lord, the supreme city of great liberation (<s>mahāmokṣa</s>). || 190

body.translated_text: Grant me the <s>samaya</s> (pledge), the <s>tattva</s> (truth), and grant me <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening); grant me the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>—the triple refuge.

children.text: trir uccārya ca tān śiṣyān jñātvā sadbhaktivatsalān |
children.translated_text: Having recited this three times, and knowing those disciples to be truly devoted and affectionate,

children.text: pradhānaṃ śiṣyam ekaṃ tu kṛtvā brūyād idaṃ vacaḥ || 191
children.translated_text: selecting one principal disciple, he should speak these words: || 191
Come, child, I shall properly teach you the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the method of the <s>mantra</s>-practice path,

children.text: deśayiṣyāmi te samyak bhājanas tvaṃ mahānaye || 192
children.translated_text: for you are a worthy vessel for the great path. || 192
The <s>Buddhas</s> born in the three times, bearers of the <s>vajra</s> of body, speech, and mind,
have attained incomparable knowledge through the power of <s>vajramantra</s>. || 193
Through the incomparable application of <s>mantra</s>, by which the great and terrible army of <s>Māra</s>,
of mighty strength, was shattered by <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> and other supreme ones. || 194
Following the ways of the world, having turned the wheel [of Dharma], they attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: tasmān matim imāṃ vatsa kuru sarvajñatāptaye || 195
children.translated_text: therefore, child, set your mind upon the attainment of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). || 195
Having recited the teaching and other [verses] three times, the <s>guru</s> should then
generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) in those in whom it has not arisen, and remind those in whom it has already arisen. || 196
Having performed protection with the all-purpose [mantra], one should meditate on the heart, throat, and crown of the head,

children.text: vajraṃ abjaṃ tathā cakraṃ hūṃ āḥ oṃ teṣu vinyaset || 197
children.translated_text: placing the <s>vajra</s>, the lotus, and the wheel [there], with [the syllables] <s>hūṃ</s>, <s>āḥ</s>, <s>oṃ</s> upon them. || 197

children.text: gandhāmbuvajrasanmuṣṭyā hūṃ oṃ āḥ evaṃ āpaṭhan |
children.translated_text: With a fist holding perfumed water and <s>vajra</s>, reciting <s>hūṃ</s> <s>oṃ</s> <s>āḥ</s>,
touching the heart, head, and throat, one should give flowers and other offerings in sequence. || 198

children.text: puṣpaṃ mūrdhni puro dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ gandhaṃ punar hṛdi |
children.translated_text: Flowers on the crown, incense before [the face], lamp and perfume again at the heart—

children.text: dadyāt sarvakṛtā japtaṃ śiṣyebhyo yatir ādarāt || 199
children.translated_text: the ascetic should give [these], consecrated with the all-purpose [mantra], to the disciples with respect. || 199
A flower-topped [stick] of twelve finger-breadths, unworm-eaten, unsplit, and unwounded,
of <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) or <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig), straight—one should give this as a tooth-cleaning stick. || 200
Having them chew it while facing east or north, one should cast [the sticks];
on ground smeared [with cow-dung] the size of a cow-hide, one should indicate accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) of pacification and other [rites]. || 201

children.text: ācamya tricalupānaṃ dattvā bāhye niveśya ca |
children.translated_text: Having rinsed the mouth, giving the three-sip libation, and establishing [the disciples] outside,
one should provide <s>kuśa</s> grass as a bed and pillow, and protect them well with arm-threads. || 202

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> for the three-sip libation:

body.text: oṃ hrīḥ viśuddhadharma sarvapāpāni cāsya śodhaya sarvavikalpān apanaya hūm ||
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ hrīḥ viśuddhadharma sarvapāpāni cāsya śodhaya sarvavikalpān apanaya hūṃ</s> (Oṃ hrīḥ, O pure dharma, purify all his sins, remove all conceptual constructions, hūṃ)

children.text: sarvajñānāṃ kadā loke sambhavo jāyate na vā |
children.translated_text: When in the world is the arising of omniscient ones born, or is it not?
Like the flower of the <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig), it occurs only very rarely. || 203
Even rarer is the arising of the path of <s>mantra</s>-practice,

children.text: yena sattvārtham atulaṃ kartuṃ śaktā hy anirvṛtāḥ || 204
children.translated_text: by which those who have not attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> are able to accomplish incomparable benefit for beings. || 204
Whatever evil was done previously over countless billions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),

children.text: tat sarvaṃ hi kṣayaṃ yāti dṛṣṭvā maṇḍalam īdṛśaṃ || 205
children.translated_text: all that is destroyed upon seeing such a <s>maṇḍala</s>. || 205
How much more so for one established in the path of <s>mantra</s>-practice of those of infinite glory—

children.text: padaṃ hy anuttaraṃ yāti japan vai mantra tāyinām || 206
children.translated_text: one attains the unsurpassed state by reciting the <s>mantras</s> of the protectors (<s>tāyins</s>). || 206
The lower realms (<s>durgati</s>) are cut off for them, [those realms] which are the source of all suffering,

children.text: yeṣāṃ caryāvare hy asmin matir atyantanirmalā || 207
children.translated_text: for those whose mind is utterly pure in this supreme practice (<s>caryā</s>). || 207

children.text: adya yuṣmābhir atulā lābhā labdhā mahātmabhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Today incomparable gains have been obtained by you, great ones,

children.text: yena yūyaṃ jinaiḥ sarvaiḥ saputrair iha śāsane || 208
children.translated_text: by which you, in the teaching of all the Victors (<s>Jinas</s>) together with their sons, || 208
have all been embraced by the great ones from the time of birth;

children.text: tena yūyaṃ mahāyāne śvo jātā hi bhaviṣyatha || 209
children.translated_text: therefore you, tomorrow, shall be born in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. || 209
This is the supreme, glorious path, the great arising of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,
by which you, traveling, shall become <s>Tathāgatas</s>. || 210
Then, having given the teaching and protection, one should put [them] to sleep on the <s>kuśa</s>-grass bed:

children.text: yat kiñcit paśyatha svapne prātar me kathayiṣyatha || 211
children.translated_text: Whatever you see in your dreams, you shall tell me in the morning. || 211
Having performed the protection-consecration and other [rites], one should recite the all-purpose [mantra];
the <s>kuṇḍalī</s> of the five families and three wheels is the all-purpose [mantra]. || 212
Having asked about the auspicious or inauspicious dream, having destroyed the inauspicious with <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>,

children.text: śiṣyān saṃrakṣya tān yogyān saṃvaraṃ grāhayet tataḥ || 213
children.translated_text: having protected those worthy disciples, one should then cause them to take the <s>saṃvara</s> (vow). || 213
Having given the <s>avaivartyasaṃseka</s> (irreversible consecration) in the <s>cakra</s> (wheel-circle), 'O Lord, tell me
the truth of the <s>cakra</s> (wheel-circle) and the deities, and the preparation of the <s>ācārya</s> (master).' || 214
The <s>samaya</s> (pledge) of all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the supreme secret <s>saṃvara</s> (vow)—
'May I always be an <s>ācārya</s> (master), for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all beings.' || 215
Having caused the disciples who seek <s>ācārya</s>-status to take the <s>saṃvara</s> (vow),

children.text: yogam ādhāya saccakraṃ saṃpūjya khe dhiyā nyaset || 216
children.translated_text: undertaking the yoga, having worshipped the true <s>cakra</s>, one should place it in space by meditation. || 216
Having the appearance free from [the extremes of] eternalism and so forth, arising from the seed-syllable of that color,
endowed with the five knowledges (<s>pañcajñāna</s>), a thread (<s>sūtra</s>) divided into twenty-five [parts], || 217
with the eyes of <s>yaḥ</s>-syllable, sun, and moon, whose body is <s>Mañjuvajra</s> himself,
drawn by the hook of blazing gaze, placed within [the area of] its own color— || 218
the knowledge-thread of the hearts of <s>Vairocana</s> and the others, together with the all-purpose [mantra],
'Grant the eternal thread, and for the stringing of your own <s>cakra</s>.' || 219
Containing the three <s>tattvas</s> (realities), up to the point of petitioning <s>Akṣobhya</s>,
recollecting 'all <s>dharmas</s> follow one another' and so forth. || 220
Square, with four doors, adorned with four <s>toraṇas</s> (gateways),
moistened with the fragrance of the five nectars (<s>pañcāmṛta</s>), and protected, || 221
the <s>yogī</s>, having entered within the three syllables, should set in motion [the thread] with the thread-holder;

children.text: trir jjaḥkārais tam āpreṣya jjaḥ jjaḥ jjaḥ ity api svayaṃ punaḥ || 222
children.translated_text: having dispatched it three times with <s>jaḥ</s>-syllables, [saying] '<s>jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ</s>,' and again himself. || 222
Holding with the left fist at the navel, standing in the western direction,
the glorious one should let fall the sky-thread, and likewise extend the thread downward. || 223

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajrasamayasūtraṃ mātikrama hūṃ</s> (Oṃ, vajra-pledge-thread, proceed in order, hūṃ)

children.translated_text: The time has come for the <s>Tathāgatas</s> pervading the sky to [work for] the welfare of beings;
one should urge them with the sound of the thread, for their coming here. || 224
Facing the directions of <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>nāga</s>-lords, supported by fire and wind,
extending the thread outward in the four directions: east, west, north, and south; || 225
having strung the diagonal thread, standing at the southeast and southwest,
[extending in] the directions east, west, north, and south—thus the eightfold <s>maṇḍala</s>. || 226

children.text: dviguṇīkṛtya tat sūtraṃ cakramadhye vidhārya ca |
children.translated_text: Having doubled that thread and placing it in the center of the <s>cakra</s>,
then the outer pair of <s>vajra</s>-threads in the shape of the <s>cakra</s>; || 227
in the northeast, the <s>cakravāḍa</s> (enclosing wall), in its proper sequence clockwise,
the wise one should string with the thread, maintaining equality in all directions. || 228

children.text: animittair asiddhiḥ syāt sūtracchede guroḥ kṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: From bad omens there is failure of accomplishment; from breaking of the thread, destruction of the <s>guru</s>;
from [the thread being] too short or too long, diseases; from confusion of directions, bewilderment of the disciples. || 229
Square, with four doors, adorned with four <s>toraṇas</s> (gateways),
furnished with four threads, decorated with silk garlands and streamers. || 230
At all the corner sections and at the junctions of the door-projections (<s>niryūha</s>),
studded with <s>vajra</s>-gems, one should string the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>. || 231
Inside that, a <s>cakra</s> (wheel) resembling the eightfold <s>maṇḍala</s>,
circular all around, with half [the measurement] of the outer <s>cakra</s>. || 232
Constructed with <s>cakra</s>-pillars and other elements, enclosed by a <s>vajra</s>-garland, auspicious;
then one should divide the door, with the wrathful gaze of the <s>hrīḥ</s>-syllable. || 233
The door is one-eighth of the <s>cakra</s>, considered to be without a platform (<s>vedikā</s>);
the projections (<s>niryūha</s>) are the measure of the door, as are the deity-panels. || 234

children.text: dvārārdhā sarvato vedī kapolaḥ pakṣakas tathā |
children.translated_text: The platform (<s>vedī</s>) is half the door on all sides, as are the cheek-walls (<s>kapola</s>) and the side-wings (<s>pakṣaka</s>);
half-garlands, garlands, moon and sun [discs], silk garlands, streamers, and panels. || 235
The dust-ground is half of that, outside the base-thread ground;
the ground of the <s>cakra</s>-pillar threads and other [elements] is equal to the dust-ground. || 236
The <s>toraṇa</s> (gateway) is three times [the height of] the door, furnished with banners and bells;
the bells are blown by the wind, the banners are at the outer corners. || 237
For the other [elements], the design is proportional to the <s>cakra</s>, as befitting their beauty.
Because [he is] the knowledge-body of the fully awakened one, the eloquent one is considered to belong to the <s>vajra</s> family. || 238
In the self-purification of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), this is his <s>cittamaṇḍala</s> (mind-circle);
having ascertained the dispositions of beings, the regulation of measurements and so forth is established.
Accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) arises from the union of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and means (<s>upāya</s>)—what use is regulation by birth and so forth? || 239
Thus, beginning from one <s>hasta</s> (cubit) up to a thousand <s>hastas</s>,

children.text: evam āsūtrya tac cakraṃ dīptadṛṣṭyā rajāṃsi tu |
children.translated_text: having thus strung that <s>cakra</s>, with blazing gaze [one should purify] the colored powders,
arousing them with the true radiance of prior-sequence knowledge, one should consecrate [them]. || 240

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajracitra samaya hūṃ</s> (Oṃ, vajra-picture, pledge, hūṃ)

children.translated_text: This <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth) is pure, the liberator of the realm of beings;
<s>Mañjurava</s> (Mañjughoṣa) himself is the king, the abode of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. || 241
Free from all faults, established within the <s>cakra</s>,

children.text: aiśānīṃ diśam āśritya gurur vāmena muṣṭinā || 242
children.translated_text: the <s>guru</s>, resorting to the northeast direction, with the left fist, || 242

children.text: śvetaṃ pītaṃ tathā raktaṃ haritaṃ kṛṣṇam eva ca |
children.translated_text: white, yellow, red, green, and black—
should let fall the lines, evenly clockwise, unbroken, and straight. || 243
One should let fall the lines evenly, with twenty divisions for the door;
from a thick stroke there will be disease; from a thin one, loss of wealth. || 244
From a crooked [line], enmity; from a broken one, death of the <s>guru</s> and disciples;
from counter-clockwise laying of the colored powders, there will be pinning down [by hostile forces]. || 245
A needle made of white <s>vajra</s> (diamond), another with a golden suspension,
a needle made of <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby), and another of <s>marakata</s> (emerald). || 246
The black [needle] should be known as the innermost—this is the sequence of colors for it.
In the east, great white; in the south, combined with yellow; || 247
the western portion is red, combined with madder [red] in the north;
the middle ground-portion is radiant with <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) [blue]. || 248
Always being of the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and means (<s>upāya</s>), one should draw with full concentration;
the lines should be laid at intervals of a barley-grain's width from each other. || 249
Crushing all evil ones with the <s>kuṇḍalī</s>-nectar-<s>vajra</s>,
the fangs proclaimed by <s>Mahāmudrā</s>, and the <s>mantrarāj</s> (mantra-king) [is the destroyer of] hostile enemies. || 250

body.text: namaḥ samantakāyavākcittavajrāṇāṃ namo vajrakrodhāya mahādaṃṣṭrotkaṭabhairavāya asimuṣalaparśupāśahastāya oṃ amṛtakuṇḍali kha 2 khāhi 2 tiṣṭha 2 bandha 2 hana 2 daha 2 garja 2 visphoṭaya 2 sarvavighnavināyakān mahāgaṇapatijīvitāntakarāya hūṃ phaṭ ||
body.translated_text: <s>namaḥ samantakāyavākcittavajrāṇāṃ namo vajrakrodhāya mahādaṃṣṭrotkaṭabhairavāya asimuṣalaparśupāśahastāya oṃ amṛtakuṇḍali kha kha khāhi khāhi tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana daha daha garja garja visphoṭaya visphoṭaya sarvavighnavināyakān mahāgaṇapatijīvitāntakarāya hūṃ phaṭ</s> (Homage to the vajras of all body, speech, and mind; homage to <s>Vajrakrodha</s>, the terrible one with great fangs, holding sword, pestle, axe, and noose in hand; Oṃ <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalī</s>, devour, devour! consume, consume! stand, stand! bind, bind! strike, strike! burn, burn! roar, roar! shatter, shatter all obstacle-creators! O ender of the life of great <s>Gaṇapati</s>, hūṃ phaṭ!)

children.translated_text: Having thus drawn the <s>maṇḍala</s>, with a seat made of moon and sun,
in the center one should draw a dark sword, radiant with perfect purity and other [qualities]. || 251
In the east, an eight-spoked <s>cakra</s> (wheel), brilliant with mirror[-like wisdom] and other [qualities];
on the left (south), a jewel (<s>ratna</s>) of green hue, with nine divisions, level and raised. || 252
In the west, an eight-petaled <s>padma</s> (lotus), red with discriminating [wisdom] and other [qualities];
in the north, a [good] sword, adorned with activity [wisdom] and other [qualities]. || 253

children.text: upāyair netram āgneyyāṃ nairṛtyāṃ vajram arthanāt |
children.translated_text: In the southeast, an eye [symbolizing] means (<s>upāya</s>); in the southwest, a <s>vajra</s> [symbolizing] purpose;

children.text: vāyavyāṃ vikaṭāsyaṃ tu balāt padmaṃ sakandakam || 254
children.translated_text: in the northwest, a gaping mouth [symbolizing] power; a lotus with stem [in another corner]. || 254
In the northeast, an <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) [symbolizing] knowledge, yellow, shining with blue luster.
In the four corners beginning from the southeast, and at both sides of the eastern door: || 255
a mirror, a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), a perfume-conch, and a bed,
a cloth, and a <s>dharmodaya</s> (dharma-source [triangle])—purified by generosity, morality, and other [perfections]. || 256
A mace [symbolizing] faith and so forth, a staff, a lotus, a <s>vajra</s>—[these are] the fourth [set];

children.text: dvāreṣu sarvathā jñātvā sphuṭaṃ dhyātvā svacakrakam || 257
children.translated_text: having fully understood [these] at the doors in every way, and having clearly meditated on one's own <s>cakra</s>, || 257

children.text: prāgvat prajñāṅgasaṃyogād buddhān svāntar niveśya ca |
children.translated_text: as before, through union with the limbs of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), having established the <s>Buddhas</s> within oneself,
pervading space with the true mind, [placing] those seated at the sides of the <s>cakra</s>, || 258
Having expelled the obstacles that came with them, and having protected [the area],
by <s>Yamāri</s> and the rest, having attracted, entered, bound [them], one should bring them under control. ||259||
Having consecrated the eye, body, and the rest, and having performed the worship of the <s>argha</s> (oblation water) and the consecration,

children.text: kṛtvā stutvātha saṃprīṇya japtvā vibhāvya toṣayet || 260
children.translated_text: having praised and then gratified [them], having recited [<s>mantras</s>] and visualized [them], one should please [them]. ||260||
As before, in the true lotus-vessel, having prepared the nectar of wisdom-<s>amṛta</s>,
having worshipped the direction-guardians established in their respective <s>yogas</s>, one should enter the <s>maṇḍala</s>. ||261||
Having become <s>Trailokyavijaya</s> (Conqueror of the Three Worlds), with ornaments and garments as obtained,
having circumambulated the wheel and bowed, one should complete [the rite] with the <s>homa</s> (fire oblation). ||262||
Leaving four finger-breadths, with a fully blossomed lotus of that measure,
a platform half a cubit below a cubit, like a wheel, serving all purposes. ||263||
From the length to the height, the sword, of the measure of eight or one finger-breadths,
in the center of the fire-pit, one should draw a wheel with jewel, lotus, and sword in the middle. ||264||
Encircled by a row of <s>vajras</s> on the outside, the yogin, facing east,
having recited [<s>mantras</s>] and protected everything, on the left the <s>argha</s> and other implements separately. ||265||
Having placed the implements and sprinkled [them], established in the self-yoga of <s>Mañjuvajra</s>,
the fire, kindled with milk-tree fuel and the like, purified by the three syllables— ||266||
having ignited [it], by the strikes of consonants, one should offer <s>kuśa</s> grass clockwise.
Arising from the <s>rūṃ</s>-seed, situated on the lotus of the primordial heart, triangular— ||267||

children.text: dhyātvā pītaṃ trivaktraṃ tu pīnaṃ prajñāngasaṅginam |
children.translated_text: having meditated on [<s>Agni</s>], yellow, with three faces, corpulent, united with the <s>prajñā</s>-limb (consort),
with a water-pitcher, gesture of fearlessness, staff, and rosary as hands—here, the fire [-deity]: ||268||

body.text:
āvāhya jñānasadvahniṃ prāgvat tritattvaṭakkinā |
abhyukṣaṇādikaṃ tasya kṛtvāsananiveśanam|| 269
body.translated_text: having invoked the true wisdom-fire, as before, with the sprinkling and the like of the three-reality gesture, having performed seat-installation. ||269||

children.translated_text: The ladle (<s>sruk</s>) and spoon (<s>sruva</s>)—below the handle, <s>vajra</s> and jewel; above that,
the ladle is four finger-breadths [wide], bearing a <s>vajra</s> excavated to two finger-breadths. ||270||
Within the four-finger <s>vajra</s>, at the end, in the form of a lotus petal;
inside, a <s>vajra</s> excavated to one finger-breadth, with a lotus petal of two finger-breadths—that is the spoon (<s>sruva</s>). ||271||
Having meditated on one's own deity's seed-syllable, blazing, in the face of the ladle and spoon,

children.text: dadyāt pūrṇāhutiṃ tasmai rephaṃ vinyasya tanmukhe || 272
children.translated_text: one should offer the full oblation to him, having placed the syllable <s>ra</s> in its mouth. ||272||

children.text: juhvīta samidho dhanyāḥ samiddhe 'gnau ghṛtaṃ tilān |
children.translated_text: One should offer into the kindled fire: fuel-sticks, grains, ghee, sesame seeds,

children.text: dūrvākhaṇdaṃ tu dadhyannaṃ kuśān vidhikramād ataḥ || 273
children.translated_text: <s>dūrvā</s> grass, a piece of curd-rice, and <s>kuśa</s> grass, in the order of the ritual procedure. ||273||
Of the true fire of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness)-wisdom, on the heart-moon, the lord arisen from <s>maṃ</s>,
having meditated on the true wheel, one should make the offering, preceded by the external worship and the like. ||274||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ agnaye svāhā</s>! — [for] the ghee.

body.text: oṃ sarvapāpadahanavajrāya sarvapāpaṃ daha svāhā || tilānām ||
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ sarvapāpadahanavajrāya sarvapāpaṃ daha svāhā</s>! — [for] the sesame seeds.
<s>Oṃ vajrāyuṣe svāhā</s>! — [for] the <s>dūrvā</s> grass.
<s>Oṃ vajrapuṣṭaye svāhā</s>! — [for] the unbroken rice grains.
<s>Oṃ sarvasampade svāhā</s>! — [for] the curd-rice.
<s>Oṃ apratihatavajrāya svāhā</s>! — [for] the <s>kuśa</s> grass.
For increase, pacification, subjugation, attraction, hostility, expulsion, and sorcery,

body.text: oṃ svāhā hoḥ jaḥ huṃ hūṃ phaṭ mantrānte cāpi codanā ||275
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ svāhā hoḥ jaḥ huṃ hūṃ phaṭ</s>—and also the incitement at the end of the <s>mantra</s>. ||275||

children.text: hṛtsattvāt svādhipāt sarvāḥ prīṇyante devatā iti |
children.translated_text: From the being in the heart, from one's own lord, all deities are gratified—

children.text: dhyāyaṃś candrādikair anyair dravyaiḥ saṃtarpya pūrvavat || 276
children.translated_text: meditating thus, with moon-[water] and other substances, one should satisfy [them] as before. ||276||
The tongue [of flame] on the wheel of the heart-moon—at the end, the full oblation likewise;
having sprinkled, offered the <s>camana</s>-<s>argha</s> (sipping-water oblation), worshipped, and praised, one should dismiss [the fire-deity]. ||277||

children.text: śeṣaṃ havyaṃ svayogātmā vahnau hutvātha taṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: The remaining oblation—the self of self-yoga—having offered it into the fire, and then likewise
having dismissed [the fire], by the previous procedure, having worshipped the wheel, one should retire. ||278||
Having first entered oneself by the procedure of disciple-entry, the accomplished one,
having completed [the rites] up to the consecration, having obtained permission from the family-lord, ||279||
the reality born of great passion, and the wheel, like a reflection—

children.text: pure śiṣyapraveśārthaṃ tattvaṃ satyaṃ ca śrāvayet || 280
children.translated_text: for the purpose of the entry of disciples, one should teach the reality and the truth. ||280||
Because of the mark of arising from space, unborn and undying, supreme,
consisting of the great <s>vajra</s>, the being—'O <s>Mañjuvajra</s> and the rest, grant me <s>siddhi</s>!' ||281||
'The supreme great <s>siddhi</s>, the sovereign presiding deity,
the king who holds all <s>vajras</s>—grant me <s>siddhi</s>, O supreme imperishable one!' ||282||
'You are faultless and eternal, O passionate one in all passion!

children.text: tattvena siddha me bhagavan mahārāgo mahārata || 283
children.translated_text: In truth, grant me <s>siddhi</s>, O Blessed One, great passion, great delight!' ||283||
'Utterly pure, foremost in all, primordially liberated, <s>Tathāgata</s>!
O <s>Samantabhadra</s>, Self of all, O <s>Bodhisattva</s>, grant me <s>siddhi</s>!' ||284||
'The supreme great <s>siddhi</s>, with the sovereign supreme <s>mudrā</s> (seal)—
grant <s>siddhi</s>, O <s>Vajra</s>! Through great exaltation, O lord of <s>vajra</s>-pride, to me!' ||285||
'Pervading the minds of all beings, established in the hearts of all beings,
the father of all beings—Desire is supreme, foremost among those of foremost commitment.' ||286||
'By the truth that the true <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) is the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (means)—

children.text: tena satyena me nātha kāmāṃs tvaṃ paripūraya || 287
children.translated_text: by that truth, O Lord, fulfill my desires!' ||287||

children.text: pratibimbasamā dharmā acchāḥ śuddhā hy anāvilāḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Dharmas</s> (phenomena) are like reflections—clear, pure, and unstained,
ungraspable and inexpressible, arisen from causes and actions.' ||288||
'Issued forth from the reality of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness)'—by this truth, in the <s>maṇḍala</s>,

children.text: pratibimbaṃ sphuṭaṃ śiṣyāḥ sarve paśyantv akalmaṣāḥ || 289
children.translated_text: may all the disciples, free from defilement, clearly see the reflection. ||289||
The disciple, [given] the general <s>saṃvara</s> (commitment), as before radiant with body and the rest,
blindfolded as stated, with the water from the all-performing pitcher, ||290||

children.text: raktāmbaraṃ tadāsyaṃ ca pṛcchet kas tvam iti priya |
children.translated_text: wearing a red garment, with face covered, one should ask: 'Who are you, O beloved?'

children.text: śiṣyeṇāpi tato vācyaṃ subhago 'ham iti priya || 291
children.translated_text: And the disciple should then reply: 'I am the fortunate one, O beloved!' ||291||
Having worshipped, with a garland in hand, at the gate, and likewise having received the offering,

children.text: yogacittaṃ samutpādya hṛdi vajraṃ hṛdā nyaset || 292
children.translated_text: having generated the yoga-mind (<s>yogacitta</s>), one should place the <s>vajra</s> in the heart with the heart[-mantra]. ||292||

body.translated_text: <s>Mantra</s>:

body.text: oṃ sarvayogacittam utpādayāmi surate samayas tvaṃ hoḥ sidhya vajra yathāsukhaṃ |
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>—I generate the mind of all <s>yoga</s>! In [the bliss of] union, you are the <s>samaya</s> (commitment). <s>Hoḥ</s>! Be accomplished, O <s>Vajra</s>, as you please!

children.translated_text: Today you shall become consecrated by all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>!

children.text: na ca tvayedam sarvatathāgataparamarahasyam amaṇḍalapraviṣṭāya vaktavyaṃ na cāśraddhātavyam iti vācyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: And you must not speak this supreme secret of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> to one who has not entered the <s>maṇḍala</s>, nor should it be disbelieved—thus it should be declared.
With the own true <s>mantras</s> of <s>Yamāri</s> and the rest, having attracted and entered [the disciple],
with the five syllables, and also thus—it should be declared at the taking of the true <s>saṃvara</s> (commitment). ||293||

body.text: adya tvaṃ sarvatathāgatakule praviṣṭaḥ | tad ahaṃ te vajrajñānam utpādayāmi yena jñānena tvaṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhīr api prāpsyasi kim utānyāḥ siddhīḥ | na ca tvayādṛṣṭamaṇḍalasya purato vaktavyaṃ | mā te samayo vyathed iti tad dhṛdi vajram āsthāpya |
body.translated_text: 'Today you have entered the family of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. I shall now generate <s>vajra</s>-<s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) in you, by which knowledge you shall attain even the <s>siddhis</s> of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, how much more other <s>siddhis</s>! And you must not speak before one who has not seen the <s>maṇḍala</s>. May your <s>samaya</s> not be violated!' Then, having placed the <s>vajra</s> in the heart:

body.text: oṃ vajrasattvaḥ svayaṃ te 'dya hṛdaye samavasthitaḥ |

children.text: nirbhidya tatkṣaṇaṃ yāyād yadi brūyā imaṃ nayam | 294
children.translated_text: at that very instant he would pierce through and depart, should you reveal this teaching.' ||294||

body.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Vajrasattva</s> himself today is established in your heart;
Situated on a lotus, blazing with the three syllables, one should give [the disciple] the five [types of] <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) to drink.

children.text: idaṃ te nārakaṃ vāri samayātikramād dahet |
children.translated_text: 'This is the water of hell—through violation of <s>samaya</s>, it would burn you;
through keeping the <s>samaya</s>, [comes] <s>siddhi</s>—drink the <s>vajra</s>-nectar-water!' ||295||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ vajrodaka ṭhaḥ</s>!
One should make him take this firm vow:

body.text:
adya prabhṛti tavāhaṃ vajrapāṇir yad ahaṃ brūyām idaṃ kuru tat tvayā kartavyaṃ na cāham avamantavyo mā te viṣamāparihāreṇa kālakriyāṃ kṛtvā narakapatanaṃ syāt |
brūyād brūhi tataḥ śiṣyān
sarvatathāgatāś cādhitiṣṭhantām vajrasattvo me āviśatu |
body.translated_text: 'From today onward, I am your <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> (vajra-holder). Whatever I tell you, "do this"—that must be done by you. And I must not be disrespected. Lest through the failure to remedy impropriety, you die and fall into hell.' He should say: 'Speak!' Then to the disciples: 'And may all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> consecrate me! May <s>Vajrasattva</s> enter me!'
Having made him recite that, in his heart—

children.translated_text: at the corner of the <s>vajra</s>-mark, in the <s>Māhendra</s> (east) direction, one should meditate on <s>hūṃ</s>, arising from <s>laṃ</s>, yellow,
the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (west), arising from <s>vaṃ</s>, white, with the sign of a water-pot, circular. ||296||
Of the <s>Vāyavya</s> (northwest), with a blue banner-sign, like a bow, arising from <s>yaṃ</s>, moving,

children.text: kāye vāci tayor haḥ āḥ pādādho jhaiḥ samujjvalaṃ || 297
children.translated_text: in the body and speech of those two, <s>haḥ</s> and <s>āḥ</s>, and below the feet, blazing with <s>jhaiḥ</s>. ||297||

body.translated_text: In the northwest, arising from <s>raṃ</s>, triangular—having kindled [the fire], one should cause it to enter the disciple. ||298||

body.text: āveśaya stobhaya ra ra ra ra cālaya 2 hūṃ haḥ āḥ jhaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Cause to enter! Shake! <s>Ra ra ra ra</s>! Move, move! <s>Hūṃ haḥ āḥ jhaiḥ</s>!'

children.text: jihvāyāṃ raktam āḥ-kāraṃ dhyātvāviṣṭaṃ punar vadet |
children.translated_text: Having meditated on a red <s>āḥ</s>-syllable on the tongue, having entered [the disciple], one should again say:

children.text: rāgavajraṃ tam ābhujya brūhi vajra śubhāśubham || 299
children.translated_text: 'Embrace the <s>Rāgavajra</s> (passion-<s>vajra</s>)! Speak, O <s>Vajra</s>, the auspicious and inauspicious!' ||299||

body.text:
tam āveśaṃ dṛdhīkurvan tiṣṭha vajreti taṃ lapet |
prakṣepayet srajaṃ cakre
body.translated_text: Strengthening that possession, one should whisper 'Abide, O <s>Vajra</s>!' and throw the garland onto the wheel.
'Accept, O <s>Vajra</s>! <s>Hoḥ</s>!'
One should bind it on the head. ||300||
'Accept this being, O greatly powerful one!'

children.translated_text: Whether the garland falls on the emblem or near the emblem, on one who has attained or not attained—

children.text: pated rucyāpi tadyogaṃ dadyād bhavyatayātha vā || 301
children.translated_text: according to inclination, one should give that <s>yoga</s> [practice], or according to fitness. ||301||

body.translated_text: Having meditated on the blazing <s>praṇava</s> (<s>oṃ</s>) in the eyes:

children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Vajrasattva</s> himself today, intent on opening the eyes,
opens them—the all-seeing one—the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-eye!' ||302||

body.translated_text: Having meditated, one should show the wheel [<s>maṇḍala</s>].

children.translated_text: Beginning with the lord of the wheel, up to <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalin</s>,
one should sprinkle the head with water, saying: '<s>Vajra</s>-consecrate!' ||303||
