One should consecrate with the crown as before, and having given the presiding deity,

children.text: hṛdi saṃgrāhya tad vajraṃ vajreṇāpy abhiṣecayet || 304
children.translated_text: having grasped that <s>vajra</s> in the heart, one should also consecrate with the <s>vajra</s>. ||304||
'Today you are consecrated by the <s>Buddhas</s> through the <s>vajra</s>-consecration;

children.text: idaṃ tat sarvabuddhatvaṃ gṛhṇa vajraṃ susiddhaye || 305
children.translated_text: this is that very Buddhahood—take the <s>vajra</s> for excellent accomplishment!' ||305||

body.translated_text: Embracing with <s>vajra</s> and bell, from one's own lord:

body.text: oṃ vajrādhipati tvām abhiṣiñcāmi tiṣṭha vajra samayas tvaṃ ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Vajrādhipati</s>! I consecrate you. Abide, O <s>Vajra</s>—you are the <s>samaya</s>!'
On the crown, by name:

body.text: oṃ vajrasattva tvām abhiṣiñcāmi vajranāmābhiṣekataḥ || he amukavajra ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Vajrasattva</s>! I consecrate you by the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration. Hail, <s>vajra</s> [so-and-so]!'

children.text: yad yad bhāti svasarvasvaṃ mukhyaṃ tan mañjurāṭ svayaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Whatever shines forth, that very self of all, principally—that is <s>Mañjurāṭ</s> (Noble <s>Mañjuśrī</s>) himself;

children.text: dharmāḥ śuddhāḥ prakṛtyā yad buddhajñānacayaḥ sa hi || 306
children.translated_text: that <s>dharmas</s> are pure by nature—that indeed is the accumulation of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>jñāna</s> (wisdom).' ||306||
'In the sovereignty of one's own wheel, the auspicious sound of the name from the beginning;
all end in "<s>vajra</s>" because of the lordship over all, joined with "<s>he</s>."' ||307||
'The purification of the water-element is <s>Akṣobhya</s>; the crown is of the nature of equanimity;
the <s>vajra</s> is of the nature of true discernment; the lord is the doer of action, the giver of meaning.' ||308||

children.text: jñānaṃ vidyātra vajraṃ syād dhātur gotraṃ vaśī hy ataḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Jñāna</s> (wisdom) is the <s>vidyā</s> (spell) here; the <s>vajra</s> would be the element, the family; the master is therefore—
vows, predictions, assurances—in the <s>vidyā</s>-consecration also, the name [is given] thus.' ||309||
'This is that very Buddhahood, established in the hand of <s>Vajrasattva</s>;
it should always be held by you too—the firm vow of the <s>Vajra</s>-holder.' ||310||

body.text: oṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhivajrasamaye tiṣṭha eṣa tvāṃ dhārayāmi hīḥ hi hi hi hi hūṃ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhivajrasamaye tiṣṭha eṣa tvāṃ dhārayāmi hīḥ hi hi hi hi hūṃ</s>!

body.text:
sarvān vajravrataṃ dattvā vajraṃ tattvena grāhayet |
anādinidhanaḥ sattvo vajrasattvo mahārataḥ |

children.translated_text: <s>Samantabhadra</s>, Self of all, lord of <s>vajra</s>-pride, the lord!' ||311||

body.translated_text: Having given the <s>vajra</s>-vow to all, one should make them grasp the <s>vajra</s> in truth: 'The being, unborn and undying, <s>Vajrasattva</s>, great delight,
Having grasped the bell in truth:

children.text: tvayāpi hi sadā dhāryā bodhir agrā jinair matā | 312
children.translated_text: by you too she should always be held—the supreme <s>bodhi</s>, as the <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors) deem it.' ||312||

body.translated_text: 'This is she who is remembered as following the sound of the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) of all <s>Buddhas</s>;
One should ring it according to its proper <s>dharma</s>. ||313||

children.translated_text: 'Existence is pure by nature, made magnificent by its own natures;
by true beings, pure by nature, the supreme existence is created.' ||314||
Having consecrated the <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great seal), with the heart[-mantras] and the mentioned practices beginning with service,
with the <s>samayas</s> (commitments) such as the form of desire and the rest, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> without error. ||315||
With those [deities] of self-experienced nature, stationed in all directions and three times,
through the <s>yoga</s> of one's own presiding deity, one should worship oneself and others. ||316||

children.text: duṣkarair niyamais tair yat sevyamānair na siddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Through difficult restraints, when served, <s>siddhis</s> are not attained;
[but] the <s>siddhis</s> born of body, speech, mind, and <s>abhijñā</s> (supernatural knowledge), including invisibility and sky-walking, are attained.' ||317||
'Therefore <s>Buddhas</s> and true beings, who practice the supreme <s>mantra</s>-conduct,
have attained the supreme, imperishable <s>Dharma</s> through the service of all desires.' ||318||
'Serving the five sense-pleasures, which have the nature of both pleasure and pain,

children.text: jñānārthī rāgiṇāṃ yogāt sādhayet sarvam eva hi || 319
children.translated_text: the seeker of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), through the <s>yoga</s> of the passionate, would accomplish absolutely everything.' ||319||
'From the accomplishment of body, speech, and mind, and whatever other [<s>siddhis</s>] are considered of lesser birth,
they are accomplished through <s>mantra</s>-recitation, by the meditations of body, speech, and mind.' ||320||

body.translated_text: As it has been said:

children.text: vajraṃ tattvena saṃgṛhya ghaṇṭāṃ dharmeṇa vādya ca |
children.translated_text: 'Having grasped the <s>vajra</s> in truth, and having rung the bell according to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: samayena mahāmudrām adhiṣṭhāya hṛdā japed iti || 321
children.translated_text: having consecrated the <s>mahāmudrā</s> with the <s>samaya</s>, one should recite with the heart[-mantra].' ||321||

body.translated_text: That has been explained.

children.translated_text: The disciple who has taken the <s>saṃvara</s> (commitment), and likewise has given the offering,
should be requested for the consecration, having bowed, with this verse: ||322||
'Just as the great festival was given to the <s>Buddhas</s> by the <s>bodhi</s>-<s>vajra</s>,
so too, for the purpose of my protection, O <s>Khavajra</s> (space-<s>vajra</s>) and the rest, bestow [it] upon me!' ||323||
The desired yogin, stationed on the eight-petaled lotus at the platform of the entrance gate,
[surrounded] by <s>Buddha</s>-wheels arising from one's own heart, pervading space in all directions and three times, ||324||
accompanied by music, incense, and the like—as before, the one to be consecrated with the <s>vidyā</s>-consecration,
one should consecrate with the great <s>vajra</s>-consecration, with this verse: ||325||
'The great <s>vajra</s>-consecration, venerated by the three realms,
born from the abode of the three secrets of all <s>Buddhas</s>—I bestow [it].' ||326||
Having given the irreversible consecration, one should show the reality of the wheel:
'It is square, because of non-inequality—from the equality of <s>Buddha</s> and non-<s>Buddha</s>; ||327||
from the non-application of oneness, difference, and the like to the <s>dharmas</s> of body, speech, mind, and reality;

children.text: tatsmṛtis tatra yā śraddhā prāgdvāraṃ bodhaye matam || 328
children.translated_text: the remembrance there, which is faith—the eastern gate is considered [to be for] awakening. ||328||
For the abandonment and non-arising of the distortions regarding the past and the future,
and then again for the arising and stability of what is truly arisen though unreal— ||329||
the western gate is the four kinds of effort: zeal, exertion, stability, and wisdom;

children.text: paścimaṃ ṛddhipādās tu dvāraṃ tatsmṛtir atra tu || 330
children.translated_text: the rear [gate] is the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power); and remembrance is here [at this] gate. ||330||
Faith, effort, mindfulness, meditation, and wisdom—the unequaled faculties and powers;

children.text: samādhir uttaraṃ tv evaṃ caturdvāraṃ smṛtīndriyaiḥ || 331
children.translated_text: <s>samādhi</s> is the northern [gate]—thus the four gates are [explained] by the faculties of mindfulness. ||331||
By the first and the other four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), there would be four gateways like arches;
the <s>Śūraṅgama</s>, <s>Gagañja</s>, and other <s>samādhis</s> are considered the balustrades.' ||332||
On the platform, throngs of attendants busy with worship-implements, holding texts and such;
whatever colorful ornaments [are there], therefore [the <s>maṇḍala</s>] fulfills all wishes. ||333||
Pervaded everywhere by the nine aspects of the true <s>dharma</s> elevated through reverence,
resounding with banners, flags, and bells stirred by the wind at the summit of the universe; ||334||
radiant in all directions with the mirror-like <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (limbs of awakening) among the knowledges,
brilliant with necklaces, half-necklaces, moons, suns, mirrors, garlands, and <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks); ||335||
with excellent pillars of jewel-wheels and the like, purified by the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣas</s>);
within that, a wheel (<s>cakra</s>) resembling [a design of] eight <s>maṇḍalas</s>; ||336||
because of the turning of the <s>Vajrayāna</s> by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times in all directions,
encircled all around by a <s>vajra</s>-thread, perfectly circular; ||337||
the five <s>saṃbuddhas</s> (fully awakened ones) are the colored surfaces, because of delighting beings through their respective knowledges;
through the purification of sense-objects and the like, by the discernment of their own characteristics; ||338||

children.text: prāg yaj jñānāmṛtaṃ pītaṃ vajriṇāṃ kalaśaṃ tu tat |
children.translated_text: the nectar-knowledge previously drunk by the <s>vajra</s>-holders — that is the vase;
the full pot is the outflow of the fullness of the [two] accumulations, moist with compassion. ||339||
That which in the <s>maṇḍala</s> is called flower, incense, great lamp, and perfume —
[these are] the delight of the blossoms of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (limbs of awakening), the torch of <s>dharma</s>, and the accumulation of fame; ||340||
<s>Dharma</s>-food is the offering; modesty and shame are the moral restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>);
beautiful singing, dancing, and instrumental music promote great bliss. ||341||
It is a city because it is the city of liberation, and a <s>maṇḍala</s> because it is the collection of essence;
having shown the truth of the wheel (<s>cakra</s>), one should teach the truth of the deities. ||342||
Through the purity of faith, vigor, mindfulness, meditation, and wisdom, it takes the form of the six true doors;
the mind holding yoga in body and the rest, perfectly pure through the purity of wisdom; ||343||
through the external purity of the six [<s>pāramitās</s>] beginning with generosity, bearing the nature of <s>Rūpavajra</s> and the like;
because of the unconditioned nature of earth-elements and the like, having the intrinsic nature of <s>Locanā</s> and the others; ||344||
from the purification of the knowledges of objects, beings, self, concepts, and activities,
the mirror-like and other knowledges, culminating in the exhaustion-knowledge, have the form of all <s>Buddhas</s>; ||345||
through the yoga of the non-arising of knowledge, shining in the form of the wheel-lord (<s>cakreśa</s>);
through the purification of the delusion regarding form and the like, [the deities appear as] the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>; ||346||
from the reversal of avarice and the like, firmly established in the supreme stages (<s>bhūmis</s>);
from the reversal of their respective opposites, the powers (<s>balas</s>) and the rest are complete and stainless; ||347||
from non-conceptualization comes profundity; from the arising of self and others comes vastness;
from profundity and vastness, the mind is considered to be of the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and means (<s>upāya</s>); ||348||
because the <s>dharmas</s> are to be individually realized, they are not established as unity, difference, or the like;
thus, when elaborated, the <s>pāramitās</s> and the rest are fruits of [dispelling] delusion. ||349||
Then, the foremost of the pledged ones, having performed the yoga with [the <s>mudrā</s>] possessing qualities as numerous as the waters of form,
the <s>ācārya</s> (master), entering here, should effect the infusion of knowledge (<s>jñānāveśa</s>). ||350||

children.text: vajreṇa padmam āsphoṭya buddhān svāntar niveśya ca |
children.translated_text: Striking the lotus with the <s>vajra</s>, establishing the <s>Buddhas</s> within himself,
stabilizing those seated on the lotus, and obtaining permission from the clan-lord — ||351||
uttering his own name, the <s>vajra</s>-natured one should radiate through the wheel-yoga;
having brought the <s>Buddhas</s> to the side of the wheel by the sounds of <s>vajra</s> and lotus — ||352||

children.text: vighnān utsārya saṃrakṣya dattvārghaṃ pratipūjya ca |
children.translated_text: having expelled obstacles, having protected, having offered <s>argha</s> (water-offering) and worshipped,
having praised, and having performed the door-ritual through the door-guardians, one should accomplish [the rite] here. ||353||
In the ritual prescribed for the consecration (<s>seka</s>), worship, and the like — the empowerment of the eyes, body, and so forth —
one should request: 'Act for the benefit of all beings, for the accomplishment of all <s>siddhis</s>!' ||354||

children.text: cakraṃ saṃlikhya samyak prāk pratiṣṭhāyāṃ tv ayaṃ vidhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having first properly drawn the wheel, for the consecration (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), this is the procedure:
for images, texts, and the like, the consecration (<s>seka</s>) extends up to the [height of a] person; ||355||
the complete <s>argha</s>-offering, canopy, and the like, as well as the protection-fire-ritual and the like that are prescribed,
[are performed] with the three-five-syllable true <s>mantras</s>, or with <s>mantras</s> previously extracted; ||356||

children.text: kārayitvā bahiḥ snānaṃ cakravartīva tat svayam |
children.translated_text: having caused the outer bathing to be performed, like a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>), that itself

children.text: uttamaṃ tattvam etad dhi prajñopāyātmakaṃ tu yat || 357
children.translated_text: is the supreme truth — namely, that which is of the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and means (<s>upāya</s>); ||357||
the water-crown is the outflow; the ripening [consists of] the <s>vajra</s>-lords;
the personal consecration (<s>pauruṣa seka</s>) is by the <s>saṃbuddhas</s>; the purification comes from the secret yoga. ||358||
Then, a <s>yoginī</s> endowed with beauty and the like, practiced in one's own wheel [-yoga],

children.text: samayasaṃvarasthāṃ tāṃ cakre mudrām adhiṣṭhya ca || 359
children.translated_text: established in the <s>samaya</s>-vow (<s>samayasaṃvara</s>) — that one, having consecrated the <s>mudrā</s> in the wheel — ||359||
having brought the host of great <s>munis</s> (sages) within the <s>vajra</s>, and [experiencing] true bliss,
pressing with the thumb and forefinger, one should cause [the <s>bodhicitta</s>] to fall into the disciple's mouth. ||360||
The disciple, firm in resolve, should drink all as the essence of <s>Vairocana</s>;

children.text: sa bhaved viśvavad viśvo 'trāho sukheti vāg bruvan || 361
children.translated_text: he becomes universal like the universe — 'here, ah, bliss!' — so the speech declares. ||361||
The glorious one, through union with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), should perceive the truth;

children.text: iyaṃ te dhāraṇī ramyā sevyā buddhaiḥ prakalpitā || 362
children.translated_text: 'This is your lovely <s>dhāraṇī</s>, to be practiced, established by the <s>Buddhas</s>; ||362||
by the method of the wheel-sequence, taste the true bliss;
in the <s>vajra</s>-cross-legged posture, gazing at the mind within the jewel.' ||363||
The <s>maṇḍala</s>, the truth of the deities, and the preparatory rites of the <s>ācārya</s> —
having discussed [these], through the secret wisdom (<s>guhyaprajñā</s>), having consecrated, one should point out the truth. ||364||

body.translated_text: As it is said:

children.text: na tathā bodhicaryādyair anyair vāpi na yaiḥ śubhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Not thus through the practice of awakening-conduct and the like, nor by other meritorious [acts] —
are all the <s>Buddhas</s> and others attained, as [they are] through the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) from this method.' ||365||

children.text: samayaṃ rakṣayed bhartuḥ saṃvaraṃ pālayet sadā |
children.translated_text: 'One should guard the pledge (<s>samaya</s>) of the Lord; one should always maintain the vow (<s>saṃvara</s>);
the five meats and the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) are to be consumed; the guardian — that is another pledge besides this.' ||366||
'The killing of a jewel-[destroyer], the slaying, all women, taking what belongs to others, and false speech —

children.text: etad dhi vidhivat rakṣyaṃ yogatantre ca yat smṛtam || 367
children.translated_text: this indeed should be properly guarded, and whatever is prescribed in the <s>Yogatantra</s>.' ||367||
Then, having become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, one should prophesy with the supreme vehicle:
the left [hand] has a heart-fist and a robe; the right is the boon-granting [gesture]. ||368||

children.text: oṃ esāhaṃ vyākaromi tvāṃ vajrasattvas tathāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ</s>! I hereby prophesy you — <s>Vajrasattva</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>!
Having rescued [you] from the miserable destinies, for the attainment of ultimate existence.' ||369||

body.text: he vajranāma tathāgata siddhaye bhūr bhūvaḥ svaḥ ||
body.translated_text: '<s>He vajranāma tathāgata siddhaye bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>!' ||

children.translated_text: Whoever is prophesied by this — that <s>mantrin</s> is the lord of all the world;

children.text: bodhāv anuttarāyāṃ hi vyākuryāt sugatair api || 370
children.translated_text: in the unsurpassed awakening, he would be prophesied even by the <s>Sugatas</s> (Buddhas). ||370||

children.text: yathā yathā hi vinayaṃ sattvā yānti svabhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: However the beings naturally come to discipline,

children.text: tathā tathā hi sattvārtham kuryād rāgādibhiḥ śuciḥ || 371
children.translated_text: just so, for the benefit of beings, one should act through passion and the like, remaining pure. ||371||
Daily, at the four junctions [of the day], endowed with the yoga of the three <s>samādhis</s>,
having become [the deity], accomplish the <s>siddhi</s>, whether ordinary or supreme, to be cultivated. ||372||
In a thousand-fold world-system (<s>dhātusāhasra</s>), [one attains] invisibility; in a two-thousand-fold, supernormal knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>);
in a three-thousand-fold, [one becomes] a <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder); a <s>vajrin</s>, lord of all the world. ||373||

children.text: śāntipuṣṭyādi yat karma tadanyad vā yad īpsitam |
children.translated_text: Whatever rite of pacification, prosperity, and the like, or whatever else is desired —
by accomplishing it through devotion to the wheel-yoga, one succeeds quickly. ||374||

body.translated_text: Thus it is said:

children.translated_text: 'All the <s>vajra</s>-lords, contemplating the truth and purpose of passion,
produce the awakening born of passion, desiring the welfare of all beings.' ||375||
'Therefore, the <s>mantrin</s> who seeks awakening — whatever activity of body, speech, and mind,

children.text: karma kuryād vidhānena sarvaṃ tad bodhaye matam || 376
children.translated_text: should perform that <s>karma</s> according to the prescribed method — all that is considered [conducive] to awakening.' ||376||
As for the entered disciples who seek the benefits —
one should give reassurance and the three pledges according to the prescribed method. ||377||
'Having seen and entered the supreme, most secret <s>maṇḍala</s>,
freed from all sins, you are now well-established. ||378||

children.text: na bhūyo maraṇaṃ vo 'sti yānād asmān mahāsukhāt |
children.translated_text: 'There is no more death for you from this vehicle of great bliss;

children.text: adhṛṣyāś cāpy abaddhāś ca ramadhvam akutobhayāḥ || 379
children.translated_text: invincible and unfettered, rejoice without fear from any quarter! ||379||
'The suffering of [cyclic] existence has ceased for you, for the complete purification of existence;
you have arisen as the foremost of the Teacher's [disciples], for the attainment of ultimate existence. ||380||

children.text: ayaṃ vaḥ satataṃ rakṣyaḥ siddhaḥ samayasaṃvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This, the perfected <s>samaya</s>-vow (<s>samayasaṃvara</s>), is to be constantly guarded by you;
the command spoken equally by all <s>Buddhas</s> is supremely eternal. ||381||

children.text: bodhicittaṃ na vai tyājyaṃ yad vajram iti mudrayā |
children.translated_text: '<s>Bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) is never to be abandoned — that which is sealed as <s>vajra</s>;
by its mere generation, one is truly a <s>Buddha</s> — of this there is no doubt. ||382||

children.text: saddharmo na pratikṣepyo na ca tyājyaḥ kadācana |
children.translated_text: 'The true <s>dharma</s> is not to be rejected, nor is it ever to be abandoned;

children.text: ajñānād vātha mohād vā na vai vivṛṇuyāt sa tu || 383
children.translated_text: whether from ignorance or from delusion — one should not disclose it [to the unworthy]. ||383||

children.text: svam ātmānaṃ parityājya tapobhir na ca pīḍayet |
children.translated_text: 'One should not give up one's own self, nor torment [oneself] with austerities;
that which is comfortable should be maintained with ease — this is the future <s>Buddha</s>. ||384||

children.text: vajraṃ ghaṇṭā ca mudrā ca na vai tyājyā kadācana |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>vajra</s>, the bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>), and the <s>mudrā</s> are never to be abandoned;
the <s>ācārya</s> (master) is not to be disdained, for he is equal to all <s>Buddhas</s>. ||385||
'Whoever disdains the <s>ācārya</s>, the <s>guru</s> equal to all <s>Buddhas</s>,
through that insult to all <s>Buddhas</s>, he would always obtain suffering. ||386||

children.text: jvarair garair viṣair rogair ḍākinyupadravair grahaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'By fevers, poisons, toxins, diseases, afflictions by <s>ḍākinīs</s>, seizures by spirits,

children.text: vighnair vināyakair ghorair mārito narakaṃ vrajet || 387
children.translated_text: by terrible obstacles and <s>vināyakas</s> (obstructors), [that person] being slain would go to hell. ||387||
'Therefore, with every effort, the great <s>guru</s>, the <s>vajrācārya</s>,
whose excellent qualities are concealed — one should never disdain. ||388||

children.text: anurūpaṃ ca te deyaṃ gurubhaktaṃ sadakṣiṇam |
children.translated_text: 'And one should give to him what is appropriate, with devotion to the <s>guru</s>, always with offerings;

children.text: tato jvarādayas tāpā na bhūyaḥ prabhavanti hi || 389
children.translated_text: then fevers and other torments will no longer prevail. ||389||

children.text: nityaṃ svasamayaḥ sādhyo nityaṃ pūjyās tathāgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One should always accomplish one's own pledge (<s>samaya</s>); the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are always to be worshipped;

children.text: nityaṃ ca gurave deyaṃ sarvabuddhasamo hy asau || 390
children.translated_text: one should always give to the <s>guru</s>, for he is equal to all <s>Buddhas</s>. ||390||

body.translated_text: 'By that giving, the accumulation of merit; from the accumulation, supreme awakening;
what is given to him is given eternally to all <s>Buddhas</s>. ||391||

children.text: adya vaḥ saphalaṃ janma yad asmin supratiṣṭhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Today your birth is fruitful, since you are well-established in this;

children.text: samāḥ samayadevānāṃ bhavitā stha na saṃśayaḥ || 392
children.translated_text: you shall become equal to the <s>samaya</s>-deities — of this there is no doubt. ||392||
firm lords of sovereignty over the great kingdom of the three realms. ||393||

body.translated_text: 'Today you are consecrated (<s>abhiṣikta</s>), O long-lived ones, by all <s>Buddhas</s> together with <s>vajra</s>-holders;

children.text: adya mārān vinirjitya praviṣṭāḥ paramaṃ puram |
children.translated_text: 'Today, having conquered <s>Māra</s>, you have entered the supreme city;

children.text: prāptam adyaiva buddhatvaṃ bhavadbhir nātra saṃśayaḥ || 394
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s> has been attained by you today — of this there is no doubt.' ||394||

children.text: iti kuruta manaḥ prasādavajraṃ svasamayam akṣayasaukhadaṃ bhajadhvam |
children.translated_text: Thus, make your minds into adamantine faith; devote yourselves to the pledge that grants imperishable bliss;

children.text: jagati laghu sukhe 'dya vajrasattvapratisamaśāśvatatām gatā bhavantaḥ || 395
children.translated_text: in the world, you have now swiftly attained the eternal state equal to <s>Vajrasattva</s> in bliss! ||395||
The disciples, bowing to the feet of the <s>guru</s>, full of genuine devotion and affection,
should say: 'We shall do exactly as you command, O Lord!' ||396||

children.text: saty eva saṃbhave teṣāṃ pratyekaṃ vāmapāṇinā |
children.translated_text: If indeed there is capacity in them, grasping each one by the left hand
with the right thumb, one should perform the pacification (<s>śānti</s>) rite according to the prescribed method. ||397||

children.text: trisaptāhutim ekāṃ vā rājño vā bhūpater atha |
children.translated_text: With three-seven oblations, or a single one, or for a king or a ruler,
having offered the oblation for the pacification of the directional guardians and of oneself, one should request the offering-fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). ||398||
For the purpose of all beings' welfare, and in all that has been heard and so forth, respectively,
in land, elephants, gold, and the like — or [request] their assistance for one's own <s>siddhi</s>. ||399||

children.text: saṃgṛhya yat tad utsṛṣṭaṃ saṃtoṣya dattadakṣiṇān |
children.translated_text: Having collected what has been released, having gratified [all] with the offering-fees given,
one should worship the wheel with all [kinds of] food and dwelling-offerings, both one's own and others'. ||400||
Having gathered suitable, excellent disciples, with various supreme long lives,
having gratified and concluded [the rite], with the three syllables ending in '<s>muḥ</s>' — ||401||
with the <s>mantra</s> beginning with '<s>ākāra</s>' and so forth, [dissolving] the supreme wheel into emptiness;

children.text: dattvārthine rajaḥ stokaṃ mahat toye rajaḥ sṛjet || 402
children.translated_text: having given a little dust to the seeker, one should cast the [remaining] dust into water. ||402||

children.text: garttāpūre pratiṣṭhāyāṃ home cakre ca yad dhanam |
children.translated_text: Whatever wealth [is used] in filling the pit, in the consecration (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), in the fire-ritual, and in the wheel —

children.text: ācāryasyaiva tat sarvam ity āha varavajradhṛk || 403
children.translated_text: all that belongs to the <s>ācārya</s> alone — so says the excellent <s>vajra</s>-holder. ||403||
Thus, this clear procedure of the wheel has been stated for the ritualist (<s>ādikarmika</s>);
but for one who has easily obtained the infusion of knowledge (<s>jñānāveśa</s>), it is explained through the infusion alone. ||404||
At the age of twelve, having induced the possession [in] a well-worshipped boy and girl,

children.text: tābhyāṃ yad racayec cakraṃ cittavākkāyikaṃ matam || 405
children.translated_text: whatever wheel they construct through those two — that is regarded as [the wheel of] mind, speech, and body. ||405||
In mind, the instruction of <s>Akṣobhya</s> and <s>Māmakī</s> is proclaimed;
in speech, <s>Pāṇḍarā</s> and <s>Amitābha</s>; in body, <s>Śāśvata</s> and <s>Locanā</s>. ||406||
From the agitation of mind, speech, and body, this construction is wondrous:
from the agitation of mind comes clairvoyance; from the agitation of speech, <s>mantra</s>-utterance; ||407||

children.text: kāyastobhāc ca khesthānaṃ stobhāveśe vidhis tv ayam |
children.translated_text: from the agitation of body, the station in space; for the agitation-possession, this is the procedure;
the consecration of <s>ācārya</s> and disciple here is established according to the former method. ||408||
One who has attained knowledge should subjugate the three wheels by mind alone;
because by that empowerment, the wheel is seen by both self and others. ||409||
Entry here is permitted; it is considered like a clear dream;
therefore it should be known as the supreme, because of the firmness of the mind-form. ||410||
For the three yogas too, the procedure for the speech-wheel and body-wheel is as before;
in their respective places, the sign of <s>Akṣobhya</s> should be [placed], for the purification of the secrets of speech and body. ||411||
Even for those who have attained mastery through the knowledge-ritual and the entry-[ritual],

children.text: cetasaiva vidhiḥ sarvas taddhīno naiva sidhyati || 412
children.translated_text: the entire procedure is by mind alone — one deficient in that does not succeed at all. ||412||
For the foremost disciples of the <s>vajrācārya</s>, whose nature delights in the outflow and the like,

children.text: manasokto vidhiḥ śreṣṭho vāṅmātreṇātra kiṃ bhavet || 413
children.translated_text: the procedure spoken by mind is the best — what could mere words accomplish here? ||413||

children.text: vṛttamātrān na buddhatvaṃ śrutamātrāc ca no bhavet |
children.translated_text: Not from mere performance comes <s>Buddhahood</s>, nor from mere hearing;

children.text: cintayāpi na yāvac ca bhāvanāto nirucyate || 413
children.translated_text: not even from reflection — it is declared to be from meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). ||413||

body.translated_text: As it is said:

children.translated_text: 'Enough of this far-ranging discourse of <s>mantra</s>-practitioners!
The mind is to be cultivated above all — from the mind arises <s>saṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening).' ||414||

body.translated_text: As it has been said:

children.text: yat phalaṃ bodhicittaṃ tad buddhajñānam anuttaram |
children.translated_text: 'That which is the fruit — <s>bodhicitta</s> — that is the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge;
of the nature of <s>Vajrasattva</s>, it is produced from the enjoyment of <s>dharma</s>.' ||415||

body.text:
prākṛtakalpanāvṛtter nānyad duḥkhaṃ bhavātmakam |
sākṣād asya virodhy evaṃ prajñopāyātma [...] 416
body.translated_text: From the covering of natural conceptual construction, there is no other suffering consisting of existence; its direct antidote is thus of the nature of wisdom and means (<s>prajñopāya</s>) [...] ||416||
